1. Confidentiality undertakings
1.1
In this Agreement "Confidential Information" shall, with respect to each Party, mean any and all information which a Party, its directors, employees, representatives or advisors, have received or shall receive in connection with the Business Purpose from the other Party (whether disclosed or obtained in writing, orally, in electronic form, by demonstration or otherwise or in other forms) which (i) by its nature should be treated confidentially or (ii) which have been marked or otherwise designated by the disclosing Party as confidential prior to or after disclosure or receipt. 1.2
In consideration of the Parties’ making available to each other Confidential Information as defined in Sub-clause 1.1, each Party hereby agrees to the following confidentiality undertakings for and on behalf of itself and for and on behalf of the Party’s employees, advisors and representatives:
• All Confidential Information received by a Party shall be held in complete confidence by such Party and by the Party’s directors, employees, advisors or representatives, and shall not without the prior written consent of the other Party be used for any purpose other than in connection with the purpose for which such Confidential Information was disclosed or received.

• The Parties shall have in effect and maintain adequate security measures to safeguard the Confidential Information from unauthorized access, disclosure, use, and/or misappropriation.
1.3
Notwithstanding Sub-clause 1.1, the obligations undertaken by a Party under this Agreement to maintain confidentiality shall not apply to the extent that the Party is or becomes under an obligation to disclose Confidential Information (i) by order of a court of competent jurisdiction, or (ii) under statutory law including according to The Danish Access to Public Administration Files Act, provided that where possible the Party shall first notify the other Party of such obligation and upon request allow the other Party to advance any defense against such obligation where appropriate. In any event, a Party shall notify the other Party of any disclosure made under this Sub-clause 1.3 promptly after disclosure.
1.4
A Party shall promptly notify the other Party of, without limitation, any unauthorized access, use, copying or disclosure of Confidential Information of which a Party becomes aware and shall use its best endeavors to terminate such access, use etc. and shall provide all reasonable assistance requested by the other Party in this connection.

NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT CLAUSE
This Non-Disclosure Agreement, dated ___ ____________, 20__, is made between Ameren Illinois Company ('Ameren Illinois') and ____________________ ('Recipient'), collectively called the 'Parties.' Ameren Illinois holds sensitive municipal customer service and account data, which it agrees to share with Recipient under strict confidentiality. The intent is for Recipient to handle all such information securely. In consideration of the mutual promises herein, the Parties stipulate that any information provided by Ameren Illinois is governed by these terms:
1. Information Receipt: Ameren Illinois will provide Recipient with customer data protected by 815 ILCS 505/2HH ('Confidential Information'), intended for use solely by Recipient and its officers, directors, agents, employees, and contractors ('Representatives') for purposes related to electric supply aggregation under 20 ILCS 3855/1-92.
2. Definition of Confidential Information: All data shared in any format—oral, written, electronic, visual, or otherwise—is presumed Confidential Information unless specifically excluded by Section 3. This includes customer-specific, non-public data and information provided before or after this Agreement's signing.
3. Exclusions: Information is not considered Confidential if: (i) Recipient already knows it prior to disclosure and can show written proof; (ii) it becomes publicly available without Recipient's wrongdoing; (iii) it is authorized for release by the customer; (iv) it is received from a third party legally entitled to disclose it; or (v) it must be disclosed to comply with Illinois aggregation laws.
4. Confidentiality Duties: Recipient must keep all Confidential Information secure, only sharing it with Representatives who need access. These Representatives must be instructed to maintain confidentiality. Recipient is accountable for any breaches by its Representatives.
5. Legal Requests: If Recipient is compelled by law or legal process to reveal Confidential Information, it must notify Ameren Illinois before disclosure, so Ameren Illinois can pursue protective measures or waive compliance.
6. Remedies: Ameren Illinois may seek injunctive or equitable relief for any breach or threatened breach, including unauthorized activities outside aggregation. These remedies are not exclusive and supplement Ameren Illinois’s legal rights.
7. Third-Party Liability and Litigation Costs: Ameren Illinois bears no liability for damages caused by Recipient’s negligence or intentional misuse of information. Recipient is not liable for Ameren Illinois’s own improper disclosures. If Ameren Illinois is sued due to Recipient or its Representatives’ actions, Recipient must reimburse litigation costs and damages, proportionate to fault. Recipient retains immunities provided by Illinois law.
8. No Additional Obligations: Ameren Illinois offers no guarantees regarding the accuracy or completeness of Confidential Information. The Agreement does not require either party to pursue further relationships or transactions.
9. Term and Termination: Either party can end the sharing of Confidential Information via written notice. However, Recipient’s duty to keep previously received information confidential survives termination. Termination may suspend Ameren Illinois’s information listing services.
10. Waiver and Amendments: Delay or failure to exercise rights does not waive them. Modifications must be in writing and signed by both Parties. This Agreement is the sole agreement on this subject.
11. Affiliates: Confidential Information disclosed by Ameren Illinois affiliates is considered as if disclosed by Ameren Illinois itself, with rights enforceable by those affiliates.
12. Governing Law: Illinois law governs this Agreement, which is considered executed and performed in Illinois.
13. Notices: All required notices must be in writing and delivered personally, by registered mail, or overnight courier to the Parties’ designated addresses.
14. Signatures: Parties confirm their authority and agreement by signing below. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by facsimile, and supersedes prior NDAs related to municipal aggregation.
CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION
A resolution authorizes the Non-Disclosure Agreement between the City of Urbana and Ameren Illinois, empowering the Mayor and City Clerk to execute and attest the agreement. The resolution passes upon City Council approval.

This Non-Disclosure Agreement (“Agreement”) is made on ___ day of ___ 20__, (“effective date”) by and between _____________________, a _____________ Corporation, (“XXXXX”) and Data Boiler Technologies, LLC., a Massachusetts corporation (“DBT”).
WHEREAS, DBT and XXX (the “Parties”) desire to engage in business related discussions and negotiations regarding a potential business relationship (“Transaction”).
WHEREAS, the Parties may provide to each other certain confidential and proprietary information in connection with the Transaction and each desires that any such information provided shall be kept confidential by the other party; and
WHEREAS, in consideration of the disclosure of such information, each party is willing to keep the other party’s information confidential in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement;
NOW, THEREFORE, DBT and XXX hereby agree as follows:
1. Confidential Information “Confidential Information” means nonpublic information that disclosing party (“Disclosing Party”) designates as being confidential or which, under the circumstances surrounding disclosure the receiving party (“Receiving Party”) should know is treated as confidential by the Disclosing Party. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, non-public information relating to released or unreleased Disclosing Party software products, the marketing or promotion of any Disclosing Party product, Disclosing Party’s business policies or practices, financial information, technical information, computer systems, infrastructure designs, data, analysis, compilations, studies or other documentation and information received from others that Disclosing Party is obligated to treat as confidential. Confidential Information disclosed to Receiving Party by any Disclosing Party, its related entities and/or agents is covered by this Agreement. Confidential Information shall not include any information that: (i) is or subsequently becomes publicly available without Receiving Party’s breach of any obligation owed to Disclosing Party; (ii) became known to Receiving Party prior to Disclosing Party’s disclosure of such information to Receiving Party; (iii) became known to Receiving Party from a source other than Disclosing Party other than by the breach of an obligation of confidentiality owed to Disclosing Party; (iv) is independently developed by Receiving Party without access to the Disclosing Party’s information, or (v) the Confidential Information is required to be disclosed pursuant to a requirement of a governmental agency or law, and the Receiving Party may disclose such information to the government agency without prior notice to the Disclosing Party.
2. Obligations Each party agrees that it shall not make use of, disseminate, or in any way disclose any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party to any person, firm, or business, except to the extent necessary for the Transaction. The existence of any business negotiations, discussions, consultations, or agreements in progress between the parties shall not be released to any form of public media, unless agreed between the parties in writing. Both parties acknowledge that the Receiving Party shall protect the secrecy of all Confidential Information, that said Confidential Information is of critical importance to the Disclosing Party, that any violation of this Agreement would seriously and irreparably impair and damage the Disclosing Party's business, and that the Recipient shall keep all Confidential Information in a fiduciary capacity for the sole benefit of the Disclosing Party. The Receiving Party agrees that it shall treat all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party with the same degree of care as it accords to its own Confidential Information, and the Receiving Party represents that it exercises reasonable care to protect its own Confidential Information. The Receiving Party agrees disclose Confidential Information only to those employees who need to know such information and certifies that such employees have previously agreed, either as a condition to employment or in order to obtain the Confidential Information, to be bound by terms and conditions substantially similar to those of this Agreement. The Receiving Party will immediately and unconditionally give written notice to the Disclosing Party of any unauthorized use or disclosure of the Confidential Information. The Receiving Party agrees to assist the Disclosing Party in remedying any such unauthorized use or disclosure of the Confidential Information.
MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
3. Return of Information Upon the request of the Disclosing Party, Receiving Party shall return all originals, copies, reproductions and summaries of Confidential Information at Disclosing Party’s request, or at Disclosing Party’s option, certify destruction of the same.
4. Injunctive Relief Receiving Party acknowledges that monetary damages may not be a sufficient remedy for unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information and that Disclosing Party shall be entitled, without waiving any other rights or remedies, to such injunctive and other equitable relief (without bond and without the necessity of showing actual monetary damages) as may be deemed proper by a court.
5. No Further Rights All Confidential Information is and shall remain the property of Disclosing Party. Nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to as granting or conferring any rights in the Confidential Information except as provided herein.
6. No Commitment. The parties expressly agree that the provision of Information hereunder and discussions held in connection with the Transaction shall not prevent either party from pursuing similar discussions with third parties or obligate either party to continue discussions with the other or to take, continue or forego any action relating to the Transaction. Any estimates or forecasts provided by either party to the other shall not constitute commitments.
7. Miscellaneous
I. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. It shall not be modified except by a written agreement dated subsequent to the date of this Agreement and signed by both parties. None of the provisions of this Agreement shall be deemed to have been waived by any act or acquiescence on the part of Disclosing Party, its agents, or employees, but only by an instrument in writing signed by an authorized officer of Disclosing Party. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other provision(s) or of the same provision on another occasion.
II. This Agreement shall be construed and controlled by the laws of the State of Massachusetts and both parties further consent to jurisdiction by the state and federal courts sitting in Boston, Massachusetts.
III. Subject to the limitations set forth in this Agreement, this Agreement will inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the parties, their successors and assigns. Neither party may assign, delegate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the other party's prior approval.
Data Boiler Technologies, LLC. XXXXX

Non-Disclosure Clause for Contract
Moscow, ___.___.2016
The Local Organizing Committee-2018, an Autonomous Non-profit Organization (the “Client”), and The Company____________________________ (the “Company”), represented by_____________________, operating under________________________________, have executed this NDA to secure The Company’s qualification for the Client’s Public Tender ______________________ (ОТ/12) (the “Project”).
1. DEFINITION OF CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION
The Company agrees to recognize as confidential any business, proprietary, internal, or secret information, materials, or samples obtained in connection with the Project—whether accessed by receipt, observation, written study, or other means—and relating to the Client or its affiliates/subsidiaries, regardless of the source (Client, affiliates, subsidiaries, or third parties acting on the Client’s behalf). Any data derived from, processed, or analyzed from such information is likewise confidential.
2. EXCLUSIONS FROM CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION
Information is not confidential if: (a) it is publicly available or becomes so without The Company’s fault; (b) The Company possessed it before receipt from the Client, supported by documentation; (c) it was provided by a third party not bound by confidentiality to the Client, with documentary evidence; or (d) it was independently developed by The Company without using the Client’s Confidential Information. The Client is not obligated to treat information from The Company as confidential under this Agreement.
3. ACCESS TO CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION
The Company may access Confidential Information starting on the “Commencement Date of the Provision of the Confidential Information” (listed in Appendix A) and continuing until either one year has elapsed or the Project ends—whichever is later. The Client retains discretion over what information to share and has no obligation to provide any particular data. The Company is required to act with integrity to safeguard Confidential Information. Specifically: (a) Disclosure is restricted to circumstances permitted by sections 5 and 6 or with the Client’s written approval; (b) Use is limited to Project-related needs and not for personal advantage; (c) All reasonable steps must be taken to avoid accidental leaks. The Company must report unauthorized access attempts, loss or shortage of information media, any event affecting the Client’s operations, and third-party misuse within 2 working days of learning about such incidents.

Only employees and authorized representatives/subcontractors—approved in writing by the Client, needing access for Project work, and having signed NDAs with terms at least as strict as this Agreement—may access Confidential Information. If disclosure is required by court order or government mandate, The Company must notify the Client promptly (unless prohibited by law). Disclosure is limited to what is necessary for compliance, and the information remains protected under the Agreement.

The obligation lasts for five years from the Commencement Date, or (if the Project exceeds one year) for five years following Project completion. If the Client designates information as a trade secret in writing, The Company must protect it indefinitely or at least for as long as it remains a trade secret.

Upon Project completion or at the Client’s request, The Company must take reasonable measures to erase Confidential Information from archives (including electronic), returning or destroying it as directed. Exceptions include: (a) keeping information needed for reporting under clause 5; (b) retaining data necessary for ongoing consulting, reporting, or disclosures related to the Project; (c) maintaining electronic backups created automatically. One securely archived legal copy may be kept. Parties should consult in good faith to agree on alternative procedures if needed.

Without written Client approval, The Company cannot disclose its role as the Client’s counterparty or associate itself with the Client or its activities (including World Cup and Confederations Cup events), except when compelled by Russian law.

The Company acknowledges potential Client losses from Agreement violations. If Confidential Information is disclosed improperly, The Company is liable for any actual, direct damages caused, as determined under the Consulting Services Agreement. Compensation does not cover lost profits or consequential damages. The Client must supply evidence of real damage for reimbursement.
11. INTERPRETATION AND AMENDMENT
Russian Federation law governs this Agreement, supplemented by principles of good faith and reasonable business conduct, recognizing Confidential Information’s importance. CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT
This Confidentiality Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into by:
Company Name: Raffles Translation Services
Address: 71 Jurong West Central 3, #07-17, The Centris, Singapore 648335. Phone: 6570 6028
(“Company”) and (“Vendor”), each referred to individually as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”
The Agreement commences on [DATE]. The Parties acknowledge and agree as follows:
1. Definitions
(a) The term “Activity” encompasses the services or tasks performed or to be performed by the Vendor as part of their engagement with the Company.
(b) An entity qualifies as an “Affiliate” of a Party if it is directly or indirectly controlled by, controls, or is under common control with that Party; specifically, this means holding at least fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests in the entity’s governance.
(c) “Confidential Information” includes all non-public details about a Party, its affiliates, or subsidiaries, such as any communications related to the Activity, or any business, financial, technical, or other information in any form, disclosed by one Party (the “Disclosing Party”) to the other (the “Receiving Party”). This information must be marked as confidential, shared in a confidential context, or reasonably understood as confidential, and covers a broad range of operational, administrative, and strategic data.
2. Handling and Use of Confidential Information
(a) Except where otherwise authorized in writing, the Receiving Party must keep all Confidential Information secret, share it only with those within its organization or its Affiliates who require access for the Activity, and ensure such persons are under similar confidentiality duties. The Receiving Party is accountable for any breaches by those it permits access.
(b) Confidential Information may not be used to inform or assist other current or prospective clients of the Receiving Party or its Representatives, unless specifically agreed in writing.
(c) The Receiving Party is required to safeguard Confidential Information by separating it from its other records and by preventing any unauthorized use or disclosure. Duplication or copying is strictly limited to what is necessary for the Activity and only with prior written approval from the Disclosing Party.
(d) The obligations in this Agreement also extend to any Affiliates or Representatives who receive Confidential Information.
(e) Any accidental or unauthorized disclosure must be immediately reported to the Disclosing Party, along with cooperation to recover and secure the information.
(f) Exceptions. The Receiving Party’s confidentiality obligations do not apply to information that was already public, becomes public through no wrongdoing, is received from a third party not bound by confidentiality, is independently created by the Receiving Party (with proof required), or is required to be disclosed by law or court order, with prior notice provided to the Disclosing Party when possible. These exceptions also apply to approved Affiliates.
(g) Ownership. Except as specifically permitted, the Receiving Party gains no rights to the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, which remains the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party and its Affiliates.
(h) No assurance is given as to the accuracy or completeness of the Confidential Information provided.
3. Enforcement
(a) Any breach or potential breach of this Agreement may result in irreparable damage to the Disclosing Party, who may seek injunctive relief as well as other legal remedies.
4. Duration of Obligations
(a) The confidentiality commitments in this Agreement survive for five (5) years from the effective date, irrespective of whether the Agreement is terminated.
(b) Upon request by the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party must return or destroy all physical embodiments of Confidential Information and confirm compliance in writing.
5. Indemnification
(a) The Receiving Party agrees to indemnify the Disclosing Party, including its personnel and Affiliates, against any losses or expenses resulting from any failure to fulfill the terms of this Agreement.
6. Miscellaneous
(a) Not enforcing a breach does not waive a Party’s right to enforce future breaches.
(b) The Agreement is binding on successors and permitted assigns; assignment requires prior written approval from the other Party, not to be unreasonably withheld.
(c) If any term is found to be unenforceable, the rest of the Agreement remains valid unless the invalid term undermines the Agreement’s main purpose.
(d) Singapore law governs this Agreement, and Singapore courts have non-exclusive jurisdiction.
(e) Nothing in this Agreement establishes a partnership or agency. This document represents the full understanding between the Parties and can only be changed in writing signed by both Parties.
(f) No binding agreement for the Vendor’s engagement exists unless a final contract is signed by both the Company and Vendor.

Excerpt from Contract: CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT
Parties:
The International Chamber of Commerce (“ICC”), a French association governed by law 1901, headquartered at 33-43 avenue du Président Wilson, 75116 Paris, France, on behalf of its International Court of Arbitration (the “ICC Court”);
and
(please check all boxes that apply to your role within the Nominations Commission and enter your name)
.............................................................................: Member of the ICC Court
.............................................................................: National Committee Nominations Commission Member
.............................................................................: Contact Person (see paragraph 18 of the ICC Note to National Committees and Groups on Arbitrator Proposals)
..............................................................................: Other individuals associated with or employed by a National Committee (excluding the Contact Person)
collectively referred to as “Party” or “Parties.”
Recognizing the inherently confidential nature of ICC Court operations, all participants, especially ICC Court members and those involved in arbitrator nominations, must uphold strict confidentiality.
The ICC Court seeks to ensure that any information disclosed to Members during their tenure or while handling arbitrator selection complies with ICC Arbitration Rules and remains protected from unauthorized access or use.
Both Parties acknowledge a duty to maintain the secrecy, commercial sensitivity, and privacy of information encountered during the Member’s service.
Members accept that a breach of these duties could seriously harm the ICC, its staff, the Court, and the reputation of ICC arbitration, potentially requiring ICC to take appropriate remedial actions.
Accordingly, the Parties agree as follows:
Article 1 – Confidential and Proprietary Data Defined
“Confidential Information” includes all forms of business, legal, technical, financial, or commercial data, provided by or on behalf of the ICC Court, unless clearly non-confidential. The format or means of disclosure does not alter its confidential status.
“Proprietary Information” refers to any data owned by ICC, whether or not it is also confidential.
Article 2 – Confidentiality Obligations and Limitations on Use
Members must:
a) not share Confidential or Proprietary Information without explicit ICC Court authorization;
b) use such information strictly for ICC Court-related activities, not for personal or third-party benefit;
c) safeguard and hold information in confidence, employing at least reasonable care;
d) refrain from modifying or deriving new uses from the information without written approval.
Additionally, Members are only allowed to reveal Confidential or Proprietary Information for conflict checks, and solely to the designated individual responsible for such checks within their organization. Members must ensure that their firm or company destroys this information immediately after the conflict check is concluded.
Article 3 – Exceptions to Confidentiality
Obligations under Article 2 do not apply if the Member can demonstrate that the information:
a) was lawfully held without confidentiality obligations before receipt from the ICC Court;
b) was legally acquired from a third party not bound by confidentiality to ICC;
c) was independently developed by the Member.
Article 4 – Making Copies
Unless otherwise directed, Members may reproduce Confidential or Proprietary Information only as needed for their duties.
Article 5 – Right to Withhold Information
ICC is not obliged to disclose any information to Members and may decide what, if any, information is shared.
Article 6 – No Transfer of Rights
This Agreement does not grant any rights or licenses in relation to ICC’s Confidential or Proprietary Information.
Article 7 – No Guarantees
The ICC Court provides information “as is”, only warranting reasonable efforts for accuracy and utility.
Article 8 – No Further Commitments
This Agreement does not create further obligations or require entering additional contracts.
Article 9 – Duration and End of Agreement
The Agreement becomes effective upon signature and may be terminated at any time by written notice. It ends automatically when the Member’s term concludes.
Article 10 – Continuing Duties
Upon Agreement termination, Members must cease using Confidential or Proprietary Information. Responsibilities under this Agreement continue indefinitely or as long as the law allows.
Article 11 – Breach and Remedies
Loss, misuse, or unauthorized use of information could seriously damage ICC interests; monetary compensation may be insufficient. ICC reserves the right to seek injunctive or other legal remedies if breaches occur.
Article 12 – Information Disposal
Within ninety days post-termination, ICC may request return or destruction of the information, to be completed within thirty days after the request and confirmed in writing.
Article 13 – Good Faith
All actions and interpretations under this Agreement must follow good faith and fair dealing principles.
Article 14 – Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
French law governs this Agreement. Disputes are to be negotiated, and if unresolved within three weeks, are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Tribunal de Grande Instance de Paris.
Article 15 – Non-Transferability
Neither Party may assign the Agreement without written consent; prior obligations remain unaffected.
Article 16 – Written Modifications Only
Amendments must be made in writing and signed by authorized representatives.
Signed and dated below by the Parties or their representatives.
Date: ..........................................
ICC Signatory
Emmanuel Jolivet Name ...............................................................
General Counsel Title ..................................................................
International Chamber of Commerce Firm/Company .................................................
Signature Signature …………………………………………

i) was available or became generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by the Contractor; or
ii) was available, or became available, to the Contractor on a non-confidential basis prior to its disclosure to the Contractor by the Company or a Company representative, but only if such information was not made available through a breach of confidentiality owed to the Company; or
iii) was requested or legally compelled (by oral questions, interrogatories, requests for information or documents, subpoena, civil or criminal investigative demand, or similar process) or is required by a regulatory body to make any disclosure which is prohibited or otherwise constrained by this Agreement, provided, however, that the Contractor shall: (A) provide the Company with prompt notice of any such request(s) so that the Company may seek an appropriate protective order or other appropriate remedy: and (B) provide reasonable assistance to the Company in obtaining any such protective order. c) Applicability to Employees and Subcontractors. The Contractor shall not disclose any Confidential Information to any of its associates, members, employees, or subcontractors, except those employees or subcontractors who are required to have the Confidential Information in order to perform their duties in connection with the evaluation and continuation of a business relationship between the Contractor and the Company. The Contractor shall inform each such individual of the proprietary nature of the Confidential Information and of the terms and obligations of this Agreement. Neither the Company nor any of its advisors or representatives shall have any liability to the Contractor or any of its representatives resulting from the Contractor’s use of the Confidential Information.
4) CONTRACTORS.
The parties are independent of each other. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create an employment or joint relationship between the parties.

The Contractor recognizes that the Company may be irreparably damaged by any breach of this Agreement and that the Company shall be entitled to seek an injunction, specific performance, or other equitable remedy to prevent such competition or disclosure, and may entitle the Company to other legal remedies, including attorneys’ fees and costs.

EXHIBIT A — NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
PROTECTED INFORMATION OF GREENWAY CONSULTING, LLC AND OREGON TRAIL ETHANOL COALITION
This NDA (the "Agreement") is dated __________, 2002, executed between Oregon Trail Ethanol Coalition, L.L.C., a Nebraska company (the "Disclosing Party"), and _______________________, a _________________________ (the "Receiving Party").
INTRODUCTION
The Disclosing and Receiving Parties are collaborating in discussions regarding the establishment of an ethanol processing plant by Oregon Trail Ethanol Coalition (the "Transaction"). These interactions grant the Receiving Party access to confidential materials belonging to both the Disclosing Party and GreenWay Consulting, LLC ("GreenWay"). A separate nondisclosure arrangement exists between the Disclosing Party and GreenWay forbidding the dissemination of GreenWay's confidential assets, contingent on the Receiving Party signing this NDA. The purpose of this Agreement is to authorize disclosure to the Receiving Party while preventing further transmission of such information. In exchange for receiving access to confidential materials of the Disclosing Party and for mutual promises herein, the Parties agree to the following legally binding terms:
AGREEMENT
1. Definition of Confidential Information.
(a) For the purposes of this Agreement, "Confidential Information" refers to all data about the Disclosing Party or its Affiliates' business, operations, finances, or outlook, regardless of format and whether documented or not. This definition encompasses (1) information relating to officers, directors, staff, shareholders, clients, suppliers, distributors, insurers, brokers, contractors, sales agents, and licensees of the Disclosing Party and its Affiliates, current or prospective; (2) proprietary inventions, discoveries, trade secrets, processes, methods, formulas, and expertise; (3) financial records, audits, budgets, and plans; and (4) data relevant to the Transaction. However, Confidential Information excludes (x) information publicly known through no fault of the Receiving Party, and (y) information lawfully obtained by the Receiving Party from a source other than the Disclosing Party or its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, shareholders, or agents, provided such third party is not bound by confidentiality to the Disclosing Party or its Affiliates at the time of disclosure. An "Affiliate" means any entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the Disclosing Party, where "control" is defined as possessing the authority to direct management or policies, either directly or indirectly, through voting rights, contracts, or otherwise.
2. Restrictions on Disclosure. Except as allowed under Section 3, the Receiving Party must not, without written authorization from the Disclosing Party, share or utilize Confidential Information for itself or for others.
3. Authorized Disclosure. Despite Section 2, the Receiving Party may:
(a) share Confidential Information with its officers, employees, and legal counsel, strictly as required to draft, negotiate, and finalize documents for the Transaction. The Receiving Party must ensure these individuals maintain confidentiality; and
(b) disclose Confidential Information only when compelled by law, but must first inform the Disclosing Party, who may participate in deciding what information, if any, is disclosed in compliance with legal mandates, including securities regulations.
4. Return of Confidential Information. If Transaction-related activities end without completion, the Receiving Party must promptly return all tangible Confidential Information to the Disclosing Party upon written request.
5. Duration. This Agreement remains in effect indefinitely.
6. Injunctive Relief. The Receiving Party acknowledges that breaches would cause irreparable harm to both the Disclosing Party and GreenWay. Therefore, either may seek injunctions to stop violations and enforce the Agreement, in addition to any other legal remedies.
7. Governing Law. Minnesota law governs this Agreement, and its interpretation, with no regard to conflict of law rules.
8. Successors and Assigns. The Agreement applies to and benefits the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assignees.
9. Assignment Prohibition. No assignments or delegations under this Agreement are valid unless approved in writing by the affected Party.
10. Severability. If any provision is found invalid by a court, the rest remain enforceable as if the invalid part were omitted.
11. Amendments. Only written, signed amendments by both Parties are effective; any oral changes are void.
12. No Waiver by Inaction. Failure by either Party to enforce strict adherence does not waive the right to demand performance in the future.
13. Notices. All notices must be written and either hand-delivered or sent via registered mail to the addresses specified:

15. Headings. Section headings are for reference only and do not affect interpretation.
16. Signing Authority. Signatories guarantee their authority to bind their respective organizations.
17. Copies. Faxed versions of the signed Agreement are valid originals.

Contract Provision: NON-COMPETE AND CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT
NON-COMPETE AND CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT
This contract (the "Agreement"), dated May 4, 2004, is established between FREESTAR TECHNOLOGY CORPORATION, a Nevada entity headquartered at Calle Fantino Falco, J.A. Baez Building, 2nd Floor, Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic (the "Buyer"), and UNICOMP, INC., a Colorado entity located at 6478 Putnam Ford Road, Suite 208, Woodstock, Georgia 30189 (the "Stockholder").
RECITALS:
On the date noted above, and pursuant to an Asset Purchase Agreement executed concurrently (the "Purchase Agreement"), involving the Buyer, UniPay, Inc. (the "Seller"), and the Stockholder, the Buyer acquires all assets and operations of the Seller related to acting as an electronic intermediary for payment processing on goods and services conducted via credit and debit cards, presently at Seller's Murphy, North Carolina facility (the "Business"), as a continuing enterprise.
The Stockholder, as the sole owner of the Seller, stands to gain significant advantages from the transactions set forth in the Purchase Agreement.
Due to its prior ownership and management, the Stockholder possesses in-depth knowledge and confidential information about the Business.
To encourage the Buyer to finalize the Purchase Agreement, the Stockholder has consented—and the Buyer has required—to enter into this Agreement.
Therefore, in light of these premises and the mutual promises found herein and in the Purchase Agreement, both parties agree as follows:
10. Restrictions.
(a) The Stockholder acknowledges: (i) the Seller’s business relationships, clientele, suppliers, technology, expertise, proprietary strategies, and operational methods have been valuable and will continue to provide the Buyer with substantial competitive leverage, and (ii) by virtue of being the sole owner and manager, the Stockholder has acquired detailed knowledge and confidential insight about the Business.
(b) For the Buyer and its affiliates’ benefit, the Stockholder agrees not to, directly or indirectly, for itself or any subsidiary, affiliate, or other entity, and only concerning the Business:
(i) from this date onward, except when legally compelled or in a legal proceeding with prior written notice to the Buyer, share, transmit, or otherwise reveal any business contacts, client lists, proprietary information, technology, trade secrets, marketing strategies, contracts, or other confidential materials belonging to the Seller or Buyer, regardless of when such information originated (excepting cases where: (A) the information is public knowledge, (B) is widely recognized in the industry, or (C) the Stockholder proves the recipient was already aware of it, not due to any breach of this or other confidentiality agreements known to the Stockholder);
(ii) during the period beginning now and ending two years from today (the "Restrictive Period"), solicit, recruit, employ, or retain (directly or indirectly, as an employee or consultant) any individual employed or retained by the Buyer at that time or within the preceding year, or otherwise substantially disrupt the Buyer’s relationship with such individuals, unless the Buyer grants written permission; and
(iii) throughout the Restrictive Period, solicit or attempt to solicit any person or entity previously serviced by the Seller or Stockholder for the purpose of offering competing or comparable services or products.
2. Remedies. Both parties agree that any violation by the Stockholder of these restrictions would cause irreparable harm to the Buyer and its affiliates, which cannot be remedied solely by monetary damages. Thus, the Buyer and its subsidiaries are entitled to seek injunctive or equitable relief, alongside any other available remedies, to enforce or prevent violations of this Agreement.
3. Legal Costs. Should a dispute arise from this Agreement, the party that prevails is entitled to reimbursement from the other party for reasonable costs and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, incurred during the dispute’s prosecution or defense.
4. Binding Effect. This Agreement is enforceable and benefits the Buyer and Stockholder, along with their subsidiaries, successors, and assigns; however, the Stockholder’s obligations hereunder cannot be assigned or delegated.
5. Governing Law and Jurisdiction. The Agreement is governed by New York law. The parties consent to exclusive jurisdiction and venue in Florida and Georgia state and federal courts for any actions relating to this Agreement.
6. Severability. The parties recognize the restrictions herein are made for fair and sufficient consideration and are reasonable in terms of duration, geography, and scope for the Buyer’s protection. These provisions are intended to be fully severable; if any restriction is found unlawful, invalid, or unenforceable in any respect, it will be modified only as necessary to ensure validity, while unaffected provisions remain in force.
7. Amendments. No term or condition of this Agreement may be waived, altered, or changed except by written agreement signed by the relevant party. A waiver in any instance does not constitute a continuing waiver or a waiver of other terms or future defaults.
8. Notices. All notices or communications required or permitted under this Agreement must be in writing and are considered delivered when personally handed over, one day after dispatch via overnight courier, or three business days after mailing via certified mail with return receipt, addressed to the party’s listed address or as updated by subsequent notice.
9. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in multiple counterparts, each considered an original, but together forming a single instrument.

WHEREAS, MaRS will be hosting a series of confidential presentations being made by entrants into a business pitch competition (the “Up-Start Competition”); and
WHEREAS, entrants into the Up-Start Competition are each in possession of certain confidential information that will be disclosed during their presentation in the competition and through questions thereafter (hereinafter "Confidential Information"); and
WHEREAS, Recipients desire to receive such Confidential Information for the purpose of participating in the Up-Start Competition either as competitors or as interested observers; and
WHEREAS, MaRS wishes to ensure that the Confidential Information provided by competitors in the Up-Start Competition remains confidential.
NOW, THEREFORE, Recipients agree as follows:
1. Recipients (and their respective partners, suppliers, licensors, licencees, agents, contractors and affiliates, who are hereby authorized to have Confidential Information disclosed to them hereunder only so long as they are in receipt of said Confidential Information under terms of confidentiality comparable to those set forth herein) hereby agree to hold in confidence any and all Confidential Information disclosed during the Up-Start Competition, either verbally or in writing. Such obligation of confidentiality shall not apply to Confidential Information:
(a) which, at the time of disclosure, is in the public domain or thereafter becomes part of the public domain by publication or otherwise, other than by breach of this Agreement by the Recipient;
(b) which was in the Recipient's possession at the time of disclosure and was not acquired, directly or indirectly, from the disclosing party;
(c) which the Recipient receives from a third party having a lawful right to disclose the same;
(d) in respect of which it can be established, by competent contemporaneous written evidence, that the same was developed by the Recipient independently of such disclosure; or
(e) which is required to be disclosed to a third party pursuant to any applicable law or decision of any court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, provided that (i) prior written notice, in light of the circumstances of such disclosure, is provided by the party required to make the disclosure to the third party to other party hereto; (ii) the party required to make the disclosure to the third party shall not disclose or release more Confidential Information than is required by law; and (iii) the party required to make disclosure to the third party cooperates with the other party hereto in any attempts it may make to obtain a protective order or other appropriate assurance that confidential treatment will be afforded to the Confidential Information.
2. Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information disclosed hereunder for any commercial or other purpose other than the purpose described in the third recital to this Agreement, without first entering into a written agreement between the parties covering such other use. Upon receiving a written request from the disclosing party, the receiving party shall cease to use the Confidential Information disclosed to it and shall promptly thereafter return to the disclosing party all written or otherwise documented Confidential Information disclosed to it pursuant to this Agreement. No copies of such Confidential Information may be retained for archival or any other purpose, unless otherwise required by law.
3. Recipient acknowledges that any violation of any of the provisions hereof by such party may result in immediate and irreparable damage to other party and agrees that in the event of such violation the other party shall, in addition to any other right, relief or remedy at law, be entitled to any equitable relief that any court of competent jurisdiction may deem just and proper.
4. Recipient agrees to use due care, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care, to keep Confidential Information disclosed to it pursuant to this Agreement in a safe and secure place that is at least as safe and secure as the place where that party keeps other confidential information that it considers to be valuable and proprietary to itself.
5. Nothing herein constitutes a license or other transfer of rights in respect of either party's interest in any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to this Agreement.
6. The obligations arising pursuant to this Agreement, including, without limitation, the parties' confidentiality obligations, shall expire on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the date first above written, unless such obligations are modified by a subsequent written agreement between the parties.
7. This Agreement shall enure to the benefit of and be binding upon the parties hereto, and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns.
8. This Agreement contains the entire agreement of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and may not be changed, modified, amended or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by the parties. The unenforceability of any provision of this Agreement shall not affect the enforceability of any other provision of this Agreement.
9. This Agreement and the rights and obligations of the parties shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Province of Ontario and the federal laws of Canada applicable therein.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives.

NON-DISCLOSURE AND CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT
 This document, titled the “Agreement,” was executed on July 16, 2002, between Shire US Inc. (“SHIRE”) and New River Pharmaceuticals Inc. (“NEW RIVER”) (previously Lotus Biochemical Corporation), with both entities collectively referred to as the “Parties.”
The Agreement outlines the terms under which SHIRE and NEW RIVER will share Confidential Information during discussions related to potential business collaborations or transactions. Confidential Information may be disclosed verbally or in writing, and is strictly intended to advance the Business Purpose. Such information must be protected from unauthorized access as stipulated by the Agreement.
Key provisions include:
1. Definitions: Confidential Information encompasses a wide range of data and materials, whether written, oral, electronic, or otherwise, relating to NEW RIVER’s proprietary technologies or either Party’s business operations. Oral disclosures must be accompanied by written confirmation within ten days.
2. Scope: The Agreement extends its protections to Confidential Information belonging to parent, subsidiary, and affiliated companies of the Parties.
3. Non-Disclosure: Each Party is obligated to maintain the confidentiality of the other’s information, exercise care in safeguarding it, refrain from unauthorized disclosure or use, and only share it for the Business Purpose unless written permission is granted.
4. Disclosure to Representatives: Confidential Information may be shared only with designated representatives with a legitimate need to know, who are bound by similar confidentiality requirements. Consultants require prior written approval for access.
5. Exceptions: Information is not considered confidential if it becomes public, is already known to the Receiving Party, is provided lawfully by a third party, is independently developed, is required to be disclosed by law, or is released with written consent.
6. Removal: Parties must not take confidential materials off the premises without approval and must comply with any conditions, including prompt return and no copying.
7. Return: Upon request, all confidential materials and copies must be returned to the Disclosing Party.
8. Notification: Any breach or unauthorized use must be reported immediately, with cooperation provided to mitigate further exposure.
9. No Rights Granted: The Agreement does not grant any licenses or rights to use Confidential Information beyond its stated purposes.
10. Limitation: Nothing in the Agreement obligates further contracts or grants intellectual property rights. If Confidential Information becomes patented or copyrighted, legal remedies are available.
11. Remedies: Unauthorized disclosure may result in immediate injunctive relief without bond and access to other legal or equitable remedies.
12. Term: The Agreement is effective for five years from July 16, 2002, unless extended in writing.
13. Notices: Notices must be in writing, sent by fax and followed by hard copy, addressed as specified.
14. Entire Agreement: This document constitutes the full agreement and may be modified only in writing.
15. Severability: Invalid provisions are replaced with enforceable ones that best reflect original intent, and unaffected provisions remain valid.
16. Governing Law: The Agreement is governed by Virginia law, and disputes are submitted to the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Virginia. The prevailing party may recover legal fees.
17. Waiver: Waivers must be explicit and do not constitute ongoing or broader waivers.
18. Authority: Each Party affirms its authority to enter into the Agreement and that terms are not in conflict with other obligations.
19. Counterparts: The Agreement may be signed in multiple copies and exchanged by fax, all of which together are binding.
Signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

(a) "Confidential Information" means non public information that the Disclosing Party either designates as being confidential or which, under the circumstances surrounding disclosure ought to be treated as confidential. "Confidential Information" includes, without limitation, information relating to released or unreleased Disclosing Party software products, the marketing or promotion of any Disclosing Party product, Disclosing Party's business policies or practices, and information received from others that Disclosing Party is obligated to treat as confidential. Confidentiality Agreement: 2017–2018 HNBA Board of Governors
This Non-Disclosure Agreement ('Agreement') is entered into as of ____________, 20__, by and between the Hispanic National Bar Association ('HNBA') and ______________________ ('Board Member'). The individuals or entities involved may be individually referred to as a 'Party' or together as the 'Parties.'
Background:
The Parties have engaged, or anticipate engaging, in confidential written and verbal exchanges ('Confidential Communications') concerning HNBA's operations. Such communications may involve non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of HNBA, which can include business and financial records, membership data, candidate details for judicial or governmental positions, technical documents, analyses, and other proprietary material. Some communications may also be protected by attorney-client privilege or the work product doctrine ('Confidential Information').
The purpose of this Agreement is to establish the terms governing the handling and protection of Confidential Information shared between the Parties.
Key Terms:
1. 'Confidential Information' encompasses:
   (a) All materials provided by HNBA to the Board Member, in written, graphic, or electronic format, that are labeled as 'confidential' or 'proprietary.'
   (a) Any oral, written, graphic, electronic or otherwise formatted information supplied to the Board Member in relation to their HNBA duties, not publicly available, such as membership lists, financial documents, personnel assessments, program records, memoranda, emails, and internal communications, including those under legal privilege.
   (c) Information given to the Board Member for the purpose of evaluating candidates for judicial or executive roles, like completed questionnaires, investigative findings, discussions, deliberations, and final determinations regarding candidate qualifications or endorsements.
   (b) Any data that identifies individuals, such as names, contact details, birthdates, social security numbers, email addresses, or any combination thereof, as provided by HNBA.
2. All Confidential Information is governed by this Agreement’s restrictions. HNBA retains sole discretion over what and how much information is disclosed and may withhold information as it sees fit. While HNBA will strive for accuracy and completeness, it makes no guarantees in these regards, and may redact details based on third-party restrictions.
Obligations:
- The Board Member is to use the Confidential Information solely for HNBA Board activities. Rights to all proprietary aspects remain with the disclosing Party.
- Disclosure to third parties is prohibited unless explicitly authorized in writing by HNBA. Personally identifiable information may not be used for direct marketing or transferred further.
- Confidential data may only be shared with employees who need it to assist the Board Member’s HNBA responsibilities and only if those individuals have agreed to be bound by this Agreement prior to access.
Exceptions:
- The Board Member is not responsible for improper use or disclosure if:
   (a) The information is or becomes public knowledge (excluding breaches of this Agreement);
   (b) The information is lawfully sourced from independent third parties prior to HNBA’s disclosure;
   (c) The Board Member had prior independent knowledge or developed the information independently for unrelated purposes;
   (d) Disclosure is legally compelled, provided the Board Member notifies HNBA within five (5) days of becoming aware and makes reasonable efforts to ensure continued confidentiality.
- No intellectual property rights are transferred by this Agreement.
Destruction and Retention:
- Once the intended use is fulfilled, the Board Member must destroy all Confidential Information at HNBA’s instruction, while HNBA retains a copy for two years after the candidate’s request is complete.
Duration and Termination:
- The Agreement lasts five (5) years from its effective date unless one Party gives thirty (30) days' written notice to terminate earlier. Ending or expiration does not release the Board Member from obligations regarding prior disclosures.
- This document constitutes the full understanding between the Parties on confidentiality matters, superseding all previous agreements or discussions, and is governed by District of Columbia law.
Remedies:
- In the event of a breach, the disclosing Party may seek specific performance or injunctive relief, and the prevailing Party in any enforcement action shall recover attorneys’ fees. Failure to exercise rights does not amount to a waiver.

Both Parties must sign to indicate acceptance, effective as of the Agreement’s stated date.

Additional Provision: The Receiving Party is prohibited from reverse engineering any materials containing the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information.

This Agreement made and entered into this 10th day of July, 1996 ("Effective Date"), by and between SHARP CORPORATION, a Japanese corporation, having its principal place of business at 22-22, Nagaike-cho, Abeno-ku, Osaka, Japan (hereinafter called "Sharp") and Hybrid Networks, Inc., an American corporation, having its principal place of business at 10161 Bubb Road, Cupertino, California 95014-4167 (hereinafter called "Hybrid Networks").
WITNESSETH:
WHEREAS, Sharp and Hybrid Networks both have as their purpose an interest in exploring a possible business relationship and in order for the parties to explore this relationship, it may be necessary for the parties to disclose certain of their proprietary and other information to each other, which information each of the parties regards as confidential. This confidential information relates to Cable Data Modem.
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties hereto agree as follows:
1. (a) All of the confidential information (hereinafter "Confidential Information"), including, without limitation, all information relating to business plans, financial or technical matters, trade secrets, designs, know-how, inventions, operations and any other information received or acquired by one party ("Receiving Party") from the other ("Disclosing Party") in the course of exploring the possible business relationship shall be in written form and marked "Confidential," with the name of the Disclosing Party and the date of disclosure. If the Confidential Information is initially disclosed orally, it shall be reduced to written form by the Disclosing Party (including the date of the oral disclosure and name of the Disclosing Party) and presented or mailed to the Receiving Party within thirty (30) days of the first oral disclosure.
(b) The Confidential Information shall remain the property of the Disclosing Party.
(c) All information disclosed which is not marked "Confidential," or not reduced to written form and marked "Confidential" if initially disclosed orally shall be considered to be non-confidential and shall not be subject to the obligations imposed by this Agreement. All Confidential Information disclosed under this Agreement shall be limited to the subject matter mentioned in the Recital. The existence and terms of this Agreement shall be treated as Confidential Information.
2. The Receiving Party shall:
(a) hold the Confidential Information in confidence and not disclose it to third parties, except in the limited cases referred to in paragraph "6"; and
(b) not use the Confidential Information for any purpose other than exploring or examining the possibility of a business relationship between the parties.
3. Either party hereto shall have the right, at any time, to terminate in writing and discussions and exchange of information in connection with the exploration of the possibilities of a business relationship between the parties without any further obligations or liabilities to the other party, other than the obligations of confidentiality hereunder, or any right or obligation relating to the Confidential Information hereunder.
4.(i) The obligations of the above paragraph "2" shall not apply to any information which:
(a) is available to the public through no breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party; or
(b) was in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to receipt from the Disclosing Party; or
(c) is received independently from a third party who is free to disclose such information to the Receiving Party; or
(d) is subsequently independently developed by the Receiving Party; or
(e) has been or is made public by the Disclosing Party, such as by commercial use or sale or by publications or patents, or otherwise; or
(f) is approved for release by written consent of the Disclosing Party.
(ii) Disclosure of Confidential Information shall not be precluded if such disclosure is pursuant to the requirement or request of a governmental agency or by operation of law. Provided, however, the Receiving Party shall promptly give a written notice to the Disclosing party so that the Disclosing Party may seek an appropriate protective order.
5. All Confidential Information delivered to and/or in the possession of the Receiving Party shall be returned or delivered to the Disclosing Party, with all copies made thereof, in whatever form, if the Disclosing Party so requests.
6. The Receiving Party agrees that the Confidential Information shall be disclosed to only those people within its respective organizations or its agents, consultants, representatives or advisors who have a need to know the information and who are obligated under terms no less restrictive than those imposed by this Agreement on the Receiving Party.
7. Each party shall have the right to refuse to accept any information under this Agreement, and nothing herein shall obligate either party to disclose to the other party any particular information. Further, each party acknowledges that no contract or agreement providing for a business relationship, of any nature, shall be deemed to exist unless and until a final definitive agreement has been executed and delivered.
8. If any official approval is required by a government authority or disclose the Confidential Information hereunder, such disclosure is subject to that approval. Both parties shall comply in all respects with applicable laws, regulations and court orders, including but not limited to laws and regulations on export control, in both parties' countries and other applicable countries.
9. Disclosure of any information under this Agreement, or otherwise, shall not be construed as granting, directly or by implication, any license under or interest of any kind in any patent, patent application, copyright or other intellectual property rights.
10. The Disclosing Party represents and warrants that it has the right to disclose the information disclosed under the terms of this Agreement and that disclosure of this information does not conflict with the terms of any agreement between the Disclosing Party and a third party.
11. The parties hereto shall not be obligated to compensate each other for the disclosure and/or use pursuant to the terms of this Agreement of any information exchanged in connection with this Agreement or the discussions between the parties.
12. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, representations and statements, whether oral or written, between the parties relating to the disclosure of the Confidential Information. The terms of this Agreement may not be changed except by subsequent written agreement duly signed by an officer of each of the parties.
13. Subject to Paragraph "4" hereof, the obligation of the Receiving Party provided in Paragraph "2" hereof shall continue for three (3) years from the date of each receipt of the Confidential Information, even after termination of this Agreement according to paragraph "3" hereof.
14. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of Japan.
15. The Receiving Party acknowledges that remedies of damages may be inadequate to protect against breach of this Agreement and the Receiving Party agrees in advance to the granting of injunctive or other equitable relief to the Disclosing Party in addition to any other remedy which may be available to the Disclosing Party.
16. The Disclosing Party does not make any representation or warranty, except as may be specifically provided in writing, as to the accuracy or completeness of the Confidential Information, or as to its utility or suitability for any purpose of the Receiving Party and the Disclosing Party expressly disclaims any right of the Receiving Party to rely thereon, or any liability to the Receiving Party resulting from the use of the Confidential Information.

Summary of Contract Provision: NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
This contract, dated July 10, 1996, is executed between SHARP CORPORATION of Osaka, Japan, and Hybrid Networks, Inc. of Cupertino, California, USA. The agreement facilitates the potential exploration of a business partnership between the two entities, specifically regarding Cable Data Modem technology, and requires the sharing of proprietary and confidential information.
Key terms include:
1. (a) Any information considered 'Confidential Information' must be in written form and clearly labeled as 'Confidential' with the disclosing party's name and disclosure date. If initially revealed verbally, the disclosing party must document and label the information as 'Confidential' and send it to the receiving party within 15 days.
(b) Ownership of all Confidential Information remains with the disclosing party.
(c) Information not properly labeled or not reduced to writing within 15 days is not considered confidential under this contract. The definition of Confidential Information is confined to what is relevant to the intended business relationship, and the agreement’s existence and terms are also confidential.
2. The receiving party agrees to:
(a) Keep all Confidential Information private, only sharing it with individuals or agents who need access and are bound by similar confidentiality terms; and
(b) Use the information solely for evaluating a potential business relationship.
3. Either party may terminate discussions at any time in writing, retaining only the ongoing confidentiality obligations described herein.
4. The confidentiality obligations do not apply to information that is public, already known to the receiving party, lawfully obtained from another source, independently developed, or made public by the disclosing party, or if disclosure is mandated by law (with prompt notice to the disclosing party to seek protective measures).
5. Upon request, all Confidential Information (and copies) must be returned or handed over to the disclosing party.
6. Disclosure is limited to those within the organization or external advisors who require access and are subject to equivalent confidentiality duties.
7. No obligation exists to exchange specific information or to enter into a business relationship absent a final agreement.
8. Any required government approvals must be obtained for disclosure, and both parties must comply with all applicable laws and regulations.
9. Sharing Confidential Information does not confer any intellectual property rights or licenses, explicit or implied.
10. The disclosing party guarantees it is authorized to disclose the information and that doing so does not breach any third-party agreements.
11. Neither party is required to compensate the other for information shared under this agreement.
12. This document supersedes all previous confidentiality agreements, and changes are only valid if made in writing and signed by both parties.
13. Subject to the exceptions above, confidentiality obligations persist for three years from each disclosure, even after termination.
14. The agreement is governed by Japanese law.
15. The receiving party agrees that injunctive or other equitable relief may be warranted for breaches, in addition to damages.
16. The disclosing party offers no guarantees regarding the accuracy or usefulness of the information, and assumes no liability for its use.
Both parties have signed to confirm their acceptance as of July 10, 1996.
Key principle: The disclosing party must clearly designate all Confidential Information.

1. Purpose of Disclosure.
The purpose of this Agreement is to permit the parties to evaluate whether to enter into a business relationship and related projects (the “Purpose”). In connection with such discussions, Sanmina may disclose Confidential Informa-tion (defined below) to Recipient.
2. Confidential Information Defined.
“Confidential Information” shall mean and include (i) samples and prototypes, (ii) all information disclosed in any form or medium (e.g., written, verbal, electronic, visual) which (a) has been identified by Sanmina as “Confidential,” “Proprietary” or other appropriate legend indicating the confidential nature of the information or (b) would reasonably be understood to be confidential. Confidential Information includes, but is not limited to, information regarding pricing, customers and prospective customers, vendors and vendor lists, costed bills of materials, processes (including but not limited to manufacturing processes), know-how, designs (including but not limited to designs of enclosures and printed circuit boards), formulae, computer programs, databases, methods of operation, sales techniques, business methods or plans, marketing plans and strategies, finances, management, plant and equipment, and any other business information relating to Sanmina, whether constituting a trade secret, proprietary information or otherwise, which has value to Sanmina and is treated by Sanmina as being confidential.
3. Information That Is Not Confidential.
Information in the following categories shall not be considered Confidential Information under this Agreement: (a) information which is in the public domain at the time of the receipt under this Agreement; (b)
information which comes into the public domain after receipt under this Agreement without a breach of this Agreement by the Recipient; (c) information which the Recipient can show was in the Recipient’s possession before the date of disclosure under this Agreement; (d) information that the Recipient can show was acquired by the Recipient from a third party who was not known by the Recipient to be under an obligation of confidence to Sanmina. 
(Note: The previous carve-out for information independently developed by Recipient without reference to Sanmina's Confidential Information has been REMOVED.)
4. Disclosure Period and Termination.
This Agreement controls Confidential Information which is disclosed from the Effective Date until terminated. Recipient’s duty of non-disclosure under this Agreement shall extend beyond the term of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the date of last disclosure. This Agreement may be terminated by either party upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other party. The parties agree that Confidential Information constituting a trade secret shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of this Agreement for so long as such Confidential Information qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law.
5. Duty to Protect.
Recipient shall protect the disclosed Confidential Information by using the same degree of care, but no less than a reasonable degree of care, to prevent the unauthorized use, dissemination or publication of the Confidential Information as the Recipient uses to protect its own Confidential Information of a similar nature. Recipient shall (i) limit access to all Confidential Information to its employees who shall reasonably require access to the Confidential Information for the purpose set forth above, (ii) shall insure that all such employees have signed a nondisclosure agreement in content substantially similar to this Agreement, (iii) shall use the Confidential Information solely in connection with the Purpose, and (iv) shall use due diligence to insure that all such persons comply with the provisions of this Agreement. Recipient shall be liable for any breach of this Agreement by its employees or representatives.
6. Court Orders.
Nothing contained in this Agreement shall restrict Recipient from disclosing Confidential Information that is required to be disclosed under any subpoena or court order provided that the Recipient provides Sanmina with prompt notice so that Sanmina may, at its expense, seek a protective order or take other appropriate measures.
7. No Further Rights or Duties Implied.
Sanmina does not warrant that the Confidential Information it discloses, either by itself or when combined with other information or when used in a particular manner, will be sufficient or suitable for the Recipient’s purposes. The Confidential Information is provided “AS IS” with all faults. Sanmina shall not be liable for the accuracy or completeness of the Confidential Information.
Nothing contained herein shall grant a license under any patent or other intellectual property right, nor shall this Agreement or any transmission of information constitute any representation or warranty to the Recipient with respect to infringement of any intellectual property rights of others.
Sanmina has no obligation under this Agreement to purchase any item or service from the Recipient.
8. Return of Confidential Information.
Within ten (10) days after any written request by Sanmina, the Recipient shall promptly return all copies of the Confidential Information except copies required for backup, disaster recovery, or business continuity and in such case the obligations hereunder shall survive until such copies are destroyed.
9. Governing Law.
This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflicts of law principles. The parties agree that the state courts of Santa Clara County, California and the federal courts located in the Northern District of the State of California shall have exclusive jurisdiction and venue to adjudicate any and all disputes arising out of or in connection with this Agreement. The parties consent to the exercise by such courts of personal jurisdiction over them and each party waives any objection it might otherwise have to venue, personal jurisdiction, inconvenience of forum, and any similar or related doctrine.
10. Remedies.
Recipient agrees that its obligations hereunder are necessary and reasonable in order to protect Sanmina and Sanmina’s business, and expressly agrees that monetary damages will be inadequate to compensate Sanmina for any breach by either party of any covenants and agreements set forth herein. Accordingly, Recipient agrees and acknowledges that any such violation or threatened violation will cause irreparable injury to Sanmina and that, in addition to any other remedies that may be available, in law, in equity or otherwise, Sanmina will be entitled to seek injunctive relief against the threatened breach of this Agreement or the continuation of any such breach, without the necessity of proving actual damages and without the necessity of posting bond.
11. Export Restrictions.
Recipient acknowledges its obligations to control access to technical data under the U.S. export laws and regulations and agrees to adhere to such laws and regulations with regard to any technical data received under this Agreement.
12. Entire Agreement.
This document contains the complete and exclusive Agreement between the parties, and it is intended to be final expression of their agreement. No promise, representation, warranty or covenant not included in this document has been or is relied upon by any party. Each party has relied upon its own examination of the warranties, representations and covenants expressly contained in the Agreement itself. No modification or amendment of this Agreement shall be of any force unless in writing executed by all parties hereto.

Wherever one party is required or permitted or required to give written notice to the other under this Agreement, such notice will be given by hand, by certified U.S. mail, return receipt requested, by overnight courier, or by fax and addressed to the appropriate officer of such party (with a copy to the Legal Department) at the address set forth in the preamble. All such notices shall be effective upon receipt. Either party may designate a different notice address from time to time upon giving five (5) days’ prior written notice thereof to the other party.

This Confidentiality Agreement (the “Agreement”) is executed as of ____________, 20__, by and between Sanmina Corporation, a Delaware company with its headquarters at 2700 N.
