1. Objective.
The purpose of this Agreement is to allow the parties to assess a potential business partnership and related projects (the “Purpose”). As part of these discussions, Sanmina may share certain Confidential Information (see definition below) with the Recipient.
2. Definition of Confidential Information.
“Confidential Information” covers (i) prototypes and samples, (ii) any data or knowledge transferred in any manner (e.g., oral, written, electronic, visual) that is marked as “Confidential,” “Proprietary,” or another suitable designation or that would reasonably be considered confidential. Such information encompasses, but is not limited to, pricing, customer and vendor information, costed bills of materials, manufacturing methods, know-how, product designs, formulas, software, databases, operational procedures, sales and marketing strategies, financials, management data, assets, and any related business information valuable to and protected by Sanmina.
3. Exclusions.
The following do not qualify as Confidential Information: (a) details already public at the time of disclosure; (b) data that enters the public domain post-disclosure without Recipient’s breach; (c) information already possessed by Recipient prior to disclosure; (d) data received lawfully from third parties not bound to Sanmina; and (e) information independently created by Recipient without leveraging Sanmina’s Confidential Information.
4. Duration and Termination.
The Agreement applies to Confidential Information shared from the effective date until the Agreement ends. Recipient’s obligation to maintain confidentiality continues for three (3) years after the last disclosure, regardless of Agreement termination, which may occur with thirty (30) days’ written notice by either party. Data qualifying as a trade secret remains protected as long as it retains trade secret status under the law.
5. Protection Measures.
Recipient must safeguard Confidential Information using at least the same care it uses for its own similar information, and not less than a reasonable standard. Access is restricted to employees needing the information for the stated Purpose, and all such employees must have signed a nondisclosure agreement comparable to this one. Recipient may only use Confidential Information for the agreed Purpose and must ensure compliance by all who access it. Recipient is responsible for any violations by its personnel or representatives.
6. Legal Disclosure.
Nothing in this Agreement prevents Recipient from releasing Confidential Information under legal compulsion, such as a subpoena or court order, provided Sanmina is promptly notified so it can pursue protective actions.
7. No Additional Rights or Obligations.
Sanmina provides the Confidential Information “AS IS,” without assurances of fitness for Recipient’s use, and is not liable for its accuracy or completeness. No rights or licenses under intellectual property are granted, nor are any warranties given regarding infringement. Sanmina is not obligated to purchase any products or services from Recipient under this Agreement.
8. Return of Materials.
Within ten (10) days of a written request by Sanmina, Recipient must return all Confidential Information, except for backup, disaster recovery, or business continuity copies, which remain protected until they are destroyed.
9. Applicable Law.
California law governs this Agreement, disregarding conflict-of-law rules. Disputes will be resolved solely in the state courts of Santa Clara County, CA, or the federal courts of the Northern District of California. Both parties consent to these courts’ jurisdiction and waive objections related to location or convenience.
10. Remedies.
Recipient acknowledges that protecting Sanmina’s interests may require more than monetary compensation and agrees that Sanmina can seek court orders (injunctive relief) to address or prevent violations of the Agreement, without having to prove actual damages or post a bond.
11. Export Compliance.
Recipient is obligated to comply with U.S. export regulations regarding any technical information received.
12. Entirety of Agreement.
This document represents the full and exclusive agreement between the parties. No external promises or representations are binding unless included here. Any amendments must be made in writing and signed by both parties.
13. Notices.
Required or permitted notices must be sent by hand delivery, certified U.S. mail, overnight courier, or fax to the designated officer and legal department of the recipient, and are effective upon receipt. Either party may change their notice address with five days’ written notice.
14. Assignment.
Neither party may transfer or assign the Agreement or its rights or obligations without the other’s written consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld.

Background
This Contract encompasses all business interactions involving the introduction of potential financiers, joint venture associates, banks, etc. to Party 1. Its terms cover any business engagement or project undertaken between Party 1 and Party 2.
Contract
In consideration of the parties’ intent to be legally bound, they agree as follows:
1. Confidential Information Definition. Subject to section 3, “Confidential Information” refers to all non-public materials or data furnished by either party in relation to activities herein. This includes disclosures made prior to the contract date, via written, electronic, oral, visual, or other means, as well as any notes or summaries created by the Receiving Party based on such information. Confidential Information specifically includes: (i) software, utilities, methodologies, solutions, designs, processes, templates, data, and related information for existing or planned products/services; (ii) financial records, business strategies, forecasts, and plans; (iii) customer lists or specifications; and (iv) other business or technical details or trade secrets. These protections apply to Confidential Information acquired in connection with this Contract on or after its Effective Date.
2. Confidentiality and Use Limitations. The parties anticipate that Confidential Information may be exchanged. The Receiving Party commits to: (i) maintain strict confidentiality, and, per this Contract, not disclose to any third party except regulated investment bodies, lawyers, accountants, or private investors personally known to the Party; such disclosures are permitted. For unknown third parties, prior written approval from the Disclosing Party must be obtained (on terms the Disclosing Party deems proper); (ii) not use Confidential Information for any purpose beyond PR activities outlined in other written agreements referencing this Contract; (iii) safeguard Confidential Information with at least the same diligence applied to its own highly confidential information, and never less than reasonable care.
3. Exceptions. Despite the above, confidentiality obligations do not extend to information the Receiving Party proves: (i) is publicly available not due to breach; (ii) is lawfully obtained from a third party not bound by confidentiality; (iii) was already possessed or known without restriction at disclosure; or (iv) is independently developed without reference to Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information.
4. Mandatory Disclosures. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information if required by law, regulation, court order, or regulatory request, disclosing only as necessary to comply. Where permitted, the Receiving Party will promptly notify the Disclosing Party and, if feasible, cooperate (at the Disclosing Party’s expense) to allow for protective measures.
5. Ownership; No Grant of Rights. All Confidential Information remains solely owned by the Disclosing Party. Except where stated herein or in referenced written agreements, no party is required to grant any license or interest in Confidential Information or related intellectual property.

Upon completion or at written request by the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party must immediately return or destroy all Confidential Information and related notes, unless retention is mandated by law or policy. Upon request, the Receiving Party shall certify compliance in writing.
7. No Guarantee; Party Obligations. No assurances regarding the completeness or accuracy of information are provided. Obligations are limited to those explicitly stated in this Contract.
8. Term. Commitments under this Contract are ongoing and specifically survive the conclusion of discussions or negotiations following written termination notice.

Clause 9 does not apply to the mere review of unpatented, uncopyrighted materials like business plans without quantifiable value, but does apply to valuable contacts introduced between parties (investors, financiers, etc).
10. Miscellaneous. This Contract represents the full understanding between the parties concerning its subject. Amendments require written, signed agreement. Custom or prior dealings do not modify the Contract. Section headings are for convenience only and do not influence interpretation. Failure to enforce any term does not constitute a waiver. Each party bears its own costs and expenses relating to this Contract and any meetings.

11.12. No party may, directly or indirectly, circumvent, compete with, interfere with, avoid, bypass, or undermine the interests of another party by entering into agreements with individuals or entities introduced in connection with the Opportunity, unless prior written consent is obtained.
11.13. Clause 11.1 applies to all joint ventures, projects, and collaborations.

Agreement Clause: Mr. Larry Addington
Addington Enterprises, Inc.
1500 North Big Run Road
Ashland, KY 41102
Dated: March 6, 1998
Dear Mr. Addington,
Your organization (inclusive of any subsidiaries or controlled entities) has requested access to information about Zeigler Coal Holding Company (collectively referred to, along with its subsidiaries and affiliates, as the "Company," "us," or "we") for the purpose of evaluating a potential acquisition (a "Possible Transaction"). In exchange for providing you with the Evaluation Materials (defined herein), you make the following commitments:
CONFIDENTIALITY OF EVALUATION MATERIALS
You are required to maintain the confidentiality of any data (whether spoken or written) shared by us, our financial advisor CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON CORPORATION ("CSFB"), or our other agents, in connection with a Possible Transaction, including any analysis, documents, or studies created by you or your representatives that reference or utilize such information (collectively, "Evaluation Materials"). You acknowledge the sensitive and competitive nature of the Evaluation Materials and agree that misuse or unauthorized disclosure could harm the Company.
"Evaluation Materials" comprises information provided in any form or medium, or collected through inspection, regardless of whether marked "confidential." However, it excludes information that (i) becomes publicly available through no fault of yours or your representatives, (ii) is received from a third party not bound by confidentiality to the Company, or (iii) is developed independently by you.
USE LIMITATIONS
You may only use the Evaluation Materials to assess a Possible Transaction. Disclosure is limited to those within your organization or your representatives who require the information for this purpose, with the expectation that you inform them of the confidential nature and require their agreement to these terms. Any additional disclosures require prior written consent from the Company. If a transaction does not occur, neither you nor your representatives may use the Evaluation Materials for any reason. You are liable for breaches by your representatives.
LEGAL REQUESTS
Should you or your representatives be compelled by legal process (such as subpoenas or court orders) to disclose Evaluation Materials, you agree to promptly notify the Company, collaborate on potential responses, and assist in seeking protective measures. If disclosure is legally mandated and no protective order is issued, you may only disclose the minimum required, ensuring efforts are made to maintain confidentiality, and you incur no liability if the disclosure was not the result of prior unauthorized sharing.
NON-DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS
Revealing your potential interest in acquiring the Company could negatively affect its business if a deal is not completed. Therefore, unless required by law, you and your representatives must not disclose the existence or terms of any discussions or negotiations regarding a Possible Transaction without the Company’s prior written approval. The definition of "person" is broad and includes corporations, government entities, associations, and individuals.
DOCUMENT RETURN
If requested by the Company, you must immediately either return or destroy all written Evaluation Materials and related documents, without retaining any copies, and confirm their destruction in writing.
RESTRICTIONS ON CONTACT AND SOLICITATION
All questions or communications during your evaluation must be directed solely through CSFB or designated Company representatives. You are prohibited from contacting Company executives or employees regarding the Possible Transaction, or soliciting third parties for joint participation, without CSFB’s prior written consent. For two years following the agreement date, you and your agents must not induce Zeigler employees to leave or hire certain Company personnel, except for those who separated from Zeigler at least 180 days before any employment-related communication with you.
STANDSTILL OBLIGATION
For two years after this Agreement’s date, you agree not to acquire or propose acquiring Company interests or assets, participate in Company governance, or take actions that could require public disclosure of a potential deal, without Board approval. During this period, you may not request amendments or waivers to these terms from the Company or its representatives.
NO WARRANTIES
While the Company and CSFB have made efforts to include relevant information in the Evaluation Materials, you acknowledge that no guarantees—express or implied—regarding their accuracy or completeness are made. Liability for use of the materials is disclaimed, except for representations in a definitive Sale Agreement. No binding obligation to complete a sale exists unless a Sale Agreement is fully executed by all parties.
You also agree that no contract for the sale of the Company is formed unless a Sale Agreement is executed and delivered by all relevant parties, and you waive any claims related to the sale unless such agreement exists. The Company and CSFB reserve the right to manage the sale process as they see fit and may negotiate or change procedures at their discretion, with no liability owed to you unless under a Sale Agreement.
REMEDIES FOR BREACH
It is understood that monetary damages alone may be inadequate if you or your representatives violate this Agreement, entitling the Company to seek specific performance and injunctive relief, in addition to all other legal and equitable remedies.
MISCELLANEOUS
This document represents the complete agreement on this subject matter. Amendments must be in writing and signed by all parties. The laws of New York State govern this Agreement. If you agree to these terms, please sign and return a copy.
Sincerely,
ZEIGLER COAL HOLDING COMPANY
By CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON CORPORATION, as Company representative
By: [Signature]
Accepted and agreed by:
ADDINGTON ENTERPRISES, INC.
By: /s/ Stephen Addington
Name: Stephen Addington

Its purpose is to facilitate the exchange of information—referred to as Evaluation Material—during discussions about a potential transaction. Both companies commit to restricting the use of shared information solely for evaluating the transaction and to prohibit any detrimental use. Disclosure of Evaluation Material to affiliates, representatives, or professional advisors (such as investment bankers, lawyers, or accountants) is permitted, provided the receiving party obtains prior written commitments from those individuals to uphold the agreement’s confidentiality provisions. The agreement outlines procedures for legally compelled disclosures, including notifying the other party so protective measures can be sought, and limits what must be disclosed to only what is legally required. It specifies certain exceptions to what constitutes Evaluation Material, details obligations regarding the return and destruction of materials if no deal is completed, and restricts sharing information about the transaction’s status except as required by law. The agreement makes clear that no binding transaction exists unless a formal definitive contract is signed, and explicitly waives claims based on preliminary agreements or negotiations. Remedies for breaches include both equitable relief (such as injunctions) and legal remedies. The agreement’s terms are governed by Delaware law and remain in force for three years from the effective date. The proposition affirms that the receiving party may share confidential information with certain third parties, including consultants, agents, and professional advisors.

Contract Provision: NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
This document, effective as of ____________, 20___, is established between CAE Inc., whose headquarters are located at 8585 Côte de Liesse Road, Saint-Laurent, Quebec, Canada, H4T 1G6 (hereinafter referred to as “CAE”), and __________________ (legal entity name), with its business address at ____________________________ (address to be filled in). The agreement pertains to the protection of proprietary and confidential information exchanged by both parties during negotiations regarding the acquisition of goods, services, or intellectual property for project _____ (project details as applicable) (the “Purpose”).
WHEREAS: The parties hereby agree to the following terms:
1. For this Agreement, “Proprietary Information” encompasses any information—written, oral, or otherwise—which the disclosing party deems significant to its operations (including, for CAE, its subsidiaries and affiliates, collectively referred to as the “CAE Group”). This includes, but is not limited to, commercial, financial, technical, and marketing data, business plans, strategic initiatives, compensation details, trade secrets, concepts, software, designs, specifications, drawings, processes, know-how, inventions, and customer, supplier, employee, or contractor information. When feasible, the disclosing party may mark such information as “Proprietary” or “Confidential” with appropriate written identifiers.
2. The recipient of any Proprietary Information:
a) must not use or reproduce the information for anything other than the stated Purpose without prior written approval from the disclosing party;
b) is required to safeguard the information with at least the same diligence it applies to its own comparable proprietary information, and in any case, with reasonable care;
c) may only share the information with its directors, officers, employees, investment advisers, legal counsel, or other agents (including, for CAE, members of the CAE Group) who need access for the Purpose, ensuring these individuals understand the information’s confidentiality and are bound by similar obligations;
d) must refrain from reverse engineering, decompiling, or disassembling any hardware or software received;
e) shall not alter, obscure, or remove copyright, ownership notices, trademarks, logos, or legends from materials obtained.
3. Except as outlined above, neither party may disclose to anyone the existence or status of discussions relating to the Purpose.
4. Nothing in this Agreement confers any rights or titles to the disclosed Proprietary Information. No licenses, including patent or copyright licenses, are granted by this Agreement or by disclosure.
5. The recipient is not responsible for disclosure or use of Proprietary Information if:
a) it was already known without breaching confidentiality;
b) it is public knowledge or enters the public domain without a breach;
c) it is independently developed by the recipient or its affiliates without utilizing the disclosed information;
d) it is lawfully obtained from another source without breach;
e) it is acquired through market analysis of products (excluding those of either party);
f) written approval is provided by the other party;
g) disclosure is legally mandated, provided the disclosing party is notified promptly to seek remedies or agree to disclosure terms.
6. Accidental disclosure is not liable if proper care equivalent to that used for the party’s own Proprietary Information is exercised.
7. In addition to other remedies, parties acknowledge that monetary damages may be insufficient for breaches; thus, the disclosing party may pursue injunctive relief, specific performance, and equitable remedies in court.
8. The Agreement is valid for one (1) year from the effective date, with automatic one-year renewals unless non-renewal is notified 30 days prior to expiration. The disclosing party may terminate the Agreement if the recipient fails to comply with its terms.
9. After termination or expiration, confidentiality provisions persist: a) for five (5) years if the disclosing party is a prospective supplier to CAE, or b) for twenty-five (25) years if CAE is the disclosing party, unless otherwise agreed or the information becomes public through no fault of the recipient. Upon termination or request, the recipient must promptly return or destroy all Proprietary Information and certify compliance within ten (10) days, though one copy may be kept in restricted legal files for dispute purposes only.
10. Each party covers its own expenses related to this Agreement.
11. No party may make commitments for the other without written consent, nor does the Agreement obligate either party to enter into further business arrangements.
12. If any clause becomes unenforceable or invalid under applicable law, the remaining provisions remain effective.
13. Failure to exercise rights does not constitute a waiver, nor does partial exercise prevent further use of those rights.
14. Rights and duties under this Agreement require written consent for transfer or assignment.
15. This document replaces all prior agreements regarding Proprietary Information and represents the complete understanding between parties.
16. The Agreement is governed by the laws of Quebec, excluding conflict of law rules, and relevant Federal laws of Canada.
17. The Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts, each considered an original; electronic or faxed signature pages are binding, with originals to be provided upon request.
18. The parties agree this Agreement is drafted in English. Les parties ont convenu de rédiger ce contrat en Anglais.
(Signatures follow)

On August 2, 2004, Bill Woo and Gateway Venture Holdings, Inc., a Nevada-based corporation (henceforth 'Gateway'), formalized an agreement to safeguard proprietary interests and set forth mutual guidelines. The agreement affirms that each party acknowledges the value of the promises and undertakings exchanged. Under the terms, parties must not share or use confidential, financial, or trade information of the other party, except with proper authority or as necessary. They are required to actively prevent their officers, employees, agents, representatives, and associates from breaching these confidentiality obligations. This duty of confidentiality persists beyond the agreement’s expiration indefinitely, unless the information enters the public domain without fault of the party. For five years from the agreement date, neither party may, without written consent, contact or communicate—directly or through intermediaries—with specific contacts introduced by the other party, including banks, clients, investors, and advisors. The agreement also imposes comprehensive obligations to maintain secrecy regarding transaction details and prohibits attempts to circumvent the other party, initiate negotiations with disclosed contacts, or share documents with unauthorized individuals (except those required to maintain confidentiality, such as legal or tax advisors). Officers, employees, agents, representatives, and associates who receive such information must be bound by countersigning the agreement. Breach of these terms may result in claims for damages and the termination of all related arrangements. The agreement binds not only the signatories but also their successors, heirs, and assigns. All disputes must be settled solely through binding arbitration in Las Vegas, Nevada, per the American Arbitration Association’s rules, with the arbitrator’s decision being final. Arbitration costs are shared equally, while each party covers its own legal fees. Disclosure of confidential information due to a contested court order is not considered a breach. The agreement may be signed in counterparts, becoming effective only when executed by all parties. Additionally, the Receiving Party must inform the Disclosing Party if compelled by law or judicial order to reveal any Confidential Information.

RECIPROCAL CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT
This Reciprocal Confidentiality Agreement ('the Agreement') is made between Convio, Inc., a company incorporated in Delaware ('Convio'), and Blackbaud, a Delaware corporation ('Potential Buyer'; together with Convio, each referred to as a 'Party' and collectively as the 'Parties'). The Agreement is effective as of the most recent signature date below.
1. Overview. In anticipation of discussions regarding a potential negotiated transaction ('Possible Transaction'), each Party (acting as 'Provider') may disclose certain 'Evaluation Material' (defined in Section 2) to the other Party (the 'Recipient') and its Representatives, subject to the terms herein. The actions to be taken, or refrained from, are also outlined in this document.
2. Key Terms.
(a) 'Evaluation Material' refers to information provided about the Provider to the Recipient or its Representatives for the purpose of considering a Possible Transaction. This includes details related to business operations, financial status, company activities, assets, and liabilities, as well as any notes, analyses, or documents prepared by the Recipient or its Representatives that incorporate or are based on such information. Evaluation Material excludes information that (i) becomes publicly accessible otherwise than through a breach by the Recipient, (ii) was already in the Recipient’s possession without confidentiality restrictions, (iii) is received from a third party not under a confidentiality duty, or (iv) is independently developed without reference to the Provider’s disclosures.
(b) 'Representatives' comprises directors, officers, employees, agents, partners, or advisors (including but not limited to attorneys, accountants, consultants, bankers, and financial advisors) of the Provider or Recipient.
(c) 'Person' encompasses the media and any entity, whether a corporation, partnership, group, or individual.
3. Use and Protection of Evaluation Material. Recipients and their Representatives must use Evaluation Material solely for assessing a Possible Transaction, maintain confidentiality, and, except as permitted in Section 5, not disclose any Evaluation Material except to those who need it for the transaction evaluation. The Recipient is accountable for its Representatives’ compliance. No license is granted beyond the usage outlined herein.
4. Non-Disclosure of Negotiations. Subject to Section 5, the Potential Buyer and its Representatives may not disclose the exchange of Evaluation Material, the occurrence of negotiations, or related terms unless Convio consents in writing. Convio retains certain disclosure rights, provided it does not reveal the Potential Buyer’s identity or specific transaction details unless required by law or fiduciary duty.
5. Required Legal Disclosure. If disclosure of Evaluation Material is compelled by legal process, the Recipient must promptly notify the Provider, supplying details of the required disclosure to enable the Provider to seek protection. In the absence of such protection, the Recipient may comply with legal obligations but must limit the disclosure and cooperate with the Provider to preserve confidentiality as much as possible.
6. Handling of Evaluation Material. If a Party chooses not to proceed with the Possible Transaction or upon Provider’s request, the Recipient must, within five business days, destroy or return all Evaluation Material and certify compliance. Confidentiality obligations persist after destruction/return.
7. Restrictions on Solicitation and Employment. For one year after the Agreement date, Recipients must not solicit or hire the Provider's officers or employees involved in the evaluation or learned about through shared materials, nor engage them as consultants for six months post-employment. General, non-targeted job postings are not prohibited.
8. Standstill Clause. For 14 months, unless otherwise invited in writing, neither Party nor its affiliates/Representatives may attempt to acquire the other, initiate public offers, seek to influence management, or coordinate actions with third parties concerning such activities. These restrictions end under defined acquisition scenarios.
9. Attorney-Client Privilege. If Evaluation Material includes privileged or work product information, sharing it does not waive applicable protections. Such information remains protected under privilege and the joint defense doctrine.
10. Securities Law Compliance. Recipients and their Representatives must not use Evaluation Material in violation of securities regulations.
11. No Binding Transaction. No agreement for a Possible Transaction exists unless a definitive contract is executed. Until such time, Parties have no obligations regarding the Possible Transaction except as specifically provided herein, and negotiations may be terminated at any time.
12. No Warranties or Obligation to Disclose. Providers make no representations as to the accuracy or completeness of Evaluation Material, and are not liable for its use or omissions. Only representations made in a final transaction agreement are binding, and Providers are not required to furnish additional information.
13. Amendments and Waiver. No provision may be modified or waived unless agreed to in writing by both Parties, referencing the specific provision.
14. Remedies for Breach. Breach of the Agreement entitles the non-breaching Party to equitable remedies, including injunctions and specific performance, in addition to legal remedies.
15. Legal Costs. If litigation arises and a breach is found, the breaching Party must pay the other’s reasonable legal expenses.
16. Governing Law and Jurisdiction. Delaware law governs this Agreement, and the Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of Delaware state and federal courts for related proceedings.
17. Severability. If any provision is deemed invalid, the remainder of the Agreement remains effective, with modifications made only as necessary to enforceability.
18. Interpretation. The Agreement is interpreted as jointly drafted, without favor to either Party.
19. Term. The Agreement lasts five years from the signature date, except for trade secret obligations, which are perpetual.

Contract clause: MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
This MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") is made by and between _____ Capital, Inc., a Delaware corporation, having its principal place of business at _______________, and ___________, having its principal place of business ________________.
WHEREAS, in the course of business the parties will share Confidential Information (as defined below) with each other, the parties agree to the following terms and conditions.
1. Confidential Information. As used herein, "Confidential Information" shall mean any and all oral and written proprietary information provided by one party (the "Provider") to the other (the "Recipient"), including but not limited to financial documents, customer lists, development plans, business plans, trade secrets, and intellectual property. "Confidential Information" does not include information that (i) is generally available to the public on the date of this agreement, (ii) becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure not otherwise permissible hereunder, (iii) was in the Recipient's possession prior to disclosure by the Provider, except to the extent that the Recipient received the information in violation of any requirement of confidentiality of which the Recipient was aware or reasonably should have been aware, or (iv) is made available to the Recipient lawfully and in good faith by a third party who Recipient reasonably believes is not under an obligation to keep such information confidential.
2. Use of Confidential Information. Each party agrees that at all times and notwithstanding any termination or expiration of this Agreement it will hold in strict confidence and not disclose to any third party Confidential Information of the other, except as approved in advance in writing by the other party to this Agreement, and will use the Confidential Information for no purpose other than evaluating or pursuing a business relationship with the other party to this Agreement.
3. Employees, Advisors, and Agents. The Recipient will only share Confidential Information with its employees, advisors, and agents when such disclosure is necessary for the purpose for which the Provider disclosed the information. All employees, advisors, and agents of the Recipient party with access to Confidential Information shall be bound by this Agreement and the Recipient shall be responsible for any unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information by its employees, advisors and/or agents.
4. Court Order. Notwithstanding the above, the Recipient shall not be in violation of this Agreement if the disclosure is in response to a valid subpoena or order by a court or other government body.
5. Care. The Recipient will use at least as much care in maintaining the confidentiality of any disclosed Information as that party uses in maintaining its own Confidential Information, and the Recipient will use at least reasonable care.
6. Notification of Loss or Disclosure. Each party shall immediately notify the other upon discovery of any loss or unauthorized disclosure of the Confidential Information of the other party.
7. Reproduction of Information. Confidential Information shall not be reproduced in any form except as required to accomplish the intent of this Agreement. Any reproduction of any Confidential Information by the Recipient shall remain the property of the Provider and shall contain any and all confidential or proprietary notices or legends that appear on the original, unless otherwise authorized in writing by the Provider.
8. Return of Information. Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, or upon written request by either party, each party shall promptly return to the other all documents and other tangible materials representing the other's Confidential Information and all copies thereof, or destroy all Confidential Information and copies thereof and certify its destruction to the Provider.
9. No Property Rights; No Partnership or Joint Venture. The parties recognize and agree that nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed as granting any property rights, by license or otherwise, to the Confidential Information of the other party disclosed pursuant to this Agreement, and any grant, if any, shall be set forth in a separate, express written agreement. Unless set forth in a separate, express written agreement, the parties hereto have not formed and are not forming a partnership or joint venture and neither party may claim otherwise.
10. Term. This Agreement shall commence on the first date that both parties have signed the Agreement (the "Effective Date") and shall terminate 3 years following the Effective Date. Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time, given that the party provides the other party with at least 90 days prior written notice. Following termination of this agreement, confidentiality shall still be maintained for two years following the termination of this Agreement.
11. State Law. This Agreement and all disputes rising hereunder shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York without regard to its conflict of laws provisions.
12. Injunctive Relief. In the event that one party breaches or threatens to breach this agreement the parties agree that monetary damages will be an inadequate remedy, and therefore, the other party will be entitled to an immediate permanent injunction against such breach and such other equitable relief as is necessary to enforce any and all of the provisions of this Agreement.
13. Interpretation. Whenever possible, each provision of this Agreement will be interpreted in such a manner as to be effective and valid under applicable law. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect under applicable law or rule in any jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability will not affect other provisions, but this Agreement will be reformed, construed, and enforced as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provisions had never been contained herein. The language in all parts of this Agreement will be construed, in all cases, according to its fair meaning, and not for or against either party hereto because one party may have drafted the Agreement.
14. Entire Agreement; No Oral Modification. This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties relating to the subject matter hereof. This Agreement is the complete, final, and exclusive embodiment of their agreement with regard to this subject matter and supersedes any prior oral discussions or written communications and agreements. This Agreement is entered into without reliance on any promise or representation other than those expressly contained herein, and it cannot be modified or amended except in writing signed by both parties.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have duly executed this Agreement effective as of the date first set forth above.

Summary of Agreement: RECIPROCAL CONFIDENTIALITY CONTRACT
This Reciprocal Confidentiality Contract (the “Contract”) is entered into by and between _____ Capital, Inc., a Delaware corporation located at _______________, and ___________, whose principal office is at ________________.
Given that both parties will exchange confidential and proprietary data as part of their business dealings, they mutually agree to the terms below:
1. Definition of Confidential Data. For the purposes of this Contract, “Confidential Information” includes all proprietary details, whether in writing or spoken, shared by one party (the “Discloser”) with the other (the “Receiver”), such as business strategies, financial information, client details, intellectual property, and development plans. However, information is not considered confidential if: (i) it is publicly accessible at the time of the agreement, (ii) it becomes public through no wrongful act, (iii) the Receiver possessed it lawfully before disclosure, unless obtained in breach of a prior obligation, or (iv) it is provided to the Receiver by a third party not bound by confidentiality.
2. Confidentiality Responsibilities. Each party commits to strictly safeguarding the other’s Confidential Information, refraining from sharing it externally unless given explicit prior written permission, and using it solely for evaluating or pursuing a business relationship under this Contract, both during and after the contract’s term.
3. Disclosure to Representatives. The Receiver may share Confidential Information with its staff, advisors, or agents only when necessary for the intended purpose. All such individuals must adhere to this Contract’s terms, and the Receiver is liable for any unauthorized leaks by them.
4. Legal Disclosure Requirement. If legally compelled (e.g., by subpoena or government order) to disclose Confidential Information, the Receiver is excused from breach provided they give the Discloser as much advance written notice as reasonably possible to allow the Discloser to seek protective measures.
5. Standard of Care. The Receiver must protect Confidential Information using at least the same degree of diligence as they use for their own confidential materials, and at minimum, reasonable care.
6. Reporting Breaches. Each party must promptly inform the other if any Confidential Information is lost or disclosed without authorization.
7. Duplication Limits. Confidential Information may not be copied except as needed to fulfill the objectives of this Contract. Any copies remain the Discloser’s property and must retain all original confidentiality markings unless otherwise permitted in writing.
8. Return or Destruction of Data. Upon the end of the Contract or upon request, both parties must swiftly return or destroy all Confidential Information and certify its destruction if requested.
9. No Rights or Business Relationship Created. Nothing in this Contract grants ownership or license rights to Confidential Information, nor does it establish a partnership or joint venture unless separately agreed in writing.
10. Term and Termination. The Contract begins once signed by both parties and lasts for three years. Either party may end it at any time with at least 90 days’ written notice. Confidentiality duties continue for two years after Contract termination.
11. Governing Law. The laws of New York State, without regard to conflict of law rules, govern this Contract and any disputes.
12. Equitable Remedies. If a party breaches or threatens breach, the other party may obtain immediate and ongoing injunctive relief, as monetary compensation is insufficient.
13. Severability and Interpretation. Each provision is to be interpreted for validity under applicable law. Invalid or unenforceable terms do not affect the remainder, and the Contract is to be interpreted fairly, not in favor of either party.
14. Final Agreement and Modification. This Contract is the sole and entire agreement on this subject, superseding any earlier discussions or agreements. It can only be altered in writing, signed by both parties.
By signing below, both parties confirm their agreement, effective as of the specified date.

Contract clause: MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
This agreement, made as of the last date set forth on the last page hereof (the “Effective Date”), by and between Ball State University (hereafter “Ball State University”) and (hereafter “Vendor”), and sets forth the terms and conditions of the disclosure and receipt of certain confidential information between the parties. The party disclosing Confidential Information, as herein defined, shall be referred to as the “Discloser” and the party receiving such “Confidential Information” shall be referred to as the “Recipient.” The term “Confidential Information” shall refer to the confidential information disclosed by any party to this Agreement.
The parties signing this document agree as follows:
a. Confidential Information may include information that is disclosed to Recipient by Discloser in any manner, whether orally, visually or in tangible form (including without limitation, documents, devices and computer readable media) and all copies thereof.
b. Tangible materials that disclose or embody Confidential Information shall be marked by Discloser as “confidential,” “proprietary” or the substantial equivalent thereof. Confidential Information disclosed orally or visually shall be identified by Discloser as confidential at the time of disclosure and promptly thereafter identified as confidential in a written document provided to Recipient.
c. Except as expressly permitted herein, for a period of one year from the effective date (Non-Disclosure Period), Recipient shall maintain in confidence and not disclose Confidential Information. Upon termination of this Agreement, Recipient’s right to use Confidential Information, shall immediately terminate.
d. Upon termination, or upon demand by Discloser at any time, or upon expiration of this Agreement, Recipient shall return promptly to Discloser or destroy, at Discloser’s option, all tangible materials that disclose or embody Confidential Information; provided, however, that Recipient may retain one copy of Discloser’s Confidential Information for archival purposes only.
e. Recipient shall have the right to use Confidential Information solely for the purpose(s) specified within this agreement [“Permitted Purpose(s)”].
f. Recipient shall disclose Confidential Information only to those of its employees who have a need to know such information for the Permitted Purpose(s).
g. Confidential Information shall not include any information that recipient can demonstrate:
1. was in Recipient’s possession without confidentiality restriction prior to disclosure by Discloser hereunder;
2. was generally known in the trade or business practiced by Discloser at the time of disclosure through no act of Recipient;
3. has come into the possession of Recipient without confidentiality restrictions from a third party and such third party is under no obligation to Discloser to maintain the confidentiality of such information; or
4. was developed by Recipient independently of and without reference to Confidential Information.
5. If a particular portion or aspect of Confidential Information becomes subject to any of the foregoing exceptions, all other portions or aspects of such information shall remain subject to all of the provisions of this Agreement.
h. Recipient agrees not to reproduce or copy by any means Confidential Information, except as reasonably required to accomplish the Permitted Purpose(s). The Confidential Information shall not be disclosed or revealed to anyone except employees of Recipient who have a need to know the information for evaluation in connection with the described Permitted Purpose(s) and who are aware of their obligations under this Agreement to maintain the Confidential Information as confidential.
i. Recipient agrees to accept the Confidential Information and to employ all reasonable efforts to maintain the Confidential Information as confidential, such efforts to be no less than the degree of care employed by Recipient to preserve and safeguard its own confidential information; provided however, that such efforts shall not be less than a reasonable degree of care.
j. Recipient shall not remove any proprietary rights legend from, and shall upon Discloser’s reasonable request, add proprietary rights legends to, materials disclosing or embodying Confidential Information.
k. Vendor acknowledges and agrees that Ball State University is a state agency subject to the provisions of the Indiana Open Records law, I.C. 5-14-et seq., and that disclosure of some or all of confidential information provided pursuant to this Agreement, and of the Agreement itself, may be compelled pursuant to that law. In the event that Recipient is required by the Indiana Open Records Act, or any other law, to disclose Discloser’s Confidential Information, Recipient shall promptly notify Discloser, consult with Discloser regarding whether there are legitimate grounds to narrow or contest such disclosure, and only disclose that information that the University, in the opinion of legal counsel, is legally obligated to disclose.
l. Discloser understands that Recipient develops and acquires technology for its own products and/or internal applications, and that existing or planned technology independently developed or acquired by Recipient may contain ideas and concepts similar or identical to those contained in Discloser’s Confidential Information. Discloser agrees that entering this Agreement shall not preclude Recipient from developing or acquiring technology similar to Discloser’s without obligations to Discloser, provided Recipient does not use the Confidential Information to develop such technology.
m. Ball State University’s Confidential Information will not be introduced in any future products marketed by the other party to this Agreement.
n. Neither party has any obligation under or by virtue of this Agreement to purchase from or furnish to the other party any products or services, or to enter into any other agreement, including but not limited to, a development, consulting, purchasing or technology licensing agreement.
o. Other than as expressly specified herein, Discloser grants no license to Recipient under any copyrights, patents, trademarks, trade secrets or other proprietary rights to use or reproduce Confidential Information. Neither party shall use or cause to be published in any kind of media or communication the name, logo or other identifying information of any of the parties to this Agreement without the prior expressed written consent of the other party.
p. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Agreement, Recipient agrees not to export, directly or indirectly, any United States (U.S.) source technical data acquired from Discloser or any products utilizing such data to any countries outside the U.S. if such export would be in violation of the United States Export Control Laws or Regulations then in effect.
q. The interpretation, application, and enforcement of this Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Indiana without reference to choice of law principles. Any claim, suit, or cause of action involving the interpretation, application, or enforcement of this Agreement shall be commenced in Delaware County Circuit Court in Muncie, Indiana.
r. This Agreement expresses the entire agreement and understanding of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior oral or written agreements, commitment and understandings pertaining to the subject matter hereof. Any modifications of or changes to this Agreement shall be in writing and signed by both parties.
s. Unless earlier terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof, this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect for the duration of the Non-Disclosure Period, whereupon it shall expire. Either party may terminate this Agreement at any time, without cause, effective immediately upon written notice of termination; however, in the event this Agreement is terminated prior to expiration of the Non-Disclosure Period, its provisions shall survive and remain in effect for the remainder of the Non-Disclosure Period, with respect to Confidential Information disclosed prior to the effective date of termination.

paraphrase.state_paraphrase:
NON-COMPETE CLAUSE: This contract, titled NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT, was executed on August 11, 1997, by TELECO ACQUISITION CORP. (the 'Company'), JON SATTERTHWAITE (the 'Shareholder'), and TELECOMM INDUSTRIES CORP. ('Parent'/'Telecomm'), a Delaware corporation. The background sets forth that the Company is purchasing Unitel, Inc.'s assets, with Satterthwaite being both an owner and executive, and will employ Satterthwaite under an Employment Agreement guaranteed by Parent. In return for these arrangements and assurances, Satterthwaite consents to the restrictions set out in this Agreement.

Section 1 defines key terms. 'Company's Affiliates' encompasses Telecomm and related entities; 'Compete' refers to a broad range of involvement in competing businesses; 'Restricted Area' includes U.S. states, Canadian provinces, and any jurisdiction where the Company or its affiliates conduct or intend to conduct business, with a minimum inclusion of Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, and Wisconsin. 'Restricted Period' spans Satterthwaite's employment and continues for at least three years post-termination, but not less than five years from the contract's date. 'Shareholder's Affiliates' covers all organizations under Satterthwaite's control or for his benefit.

Due to Satterthwaite's access to confidential information as a result of prior ownership and current employment, the Agreement prohibits him and his affiliates from engaging in competing activities within the Restricted Area during the Restricted Period. This includes soliciting or diverting business, encouraging clients to leave, or recruiting the Company’s employees. Satterthwaite affirms the fairness of these constraints and that they do not preclude livelihood, recognizing the unique and irreplaceable nature of his services. Violation prompts injunctive relief and other legal remedies.

If a breach occurs, the Restricted Period is paused and subsequently extended by the length of the violation. Each covenant is treated as independent, and if any are deemed unreasonable in scope or duration, courts may modify them to a reasonable extent without invalidating the remainder. The confidentiality terms in Section 2 are considered fundamental and enforceable regardless of other claims.

Section 2 obligates Satterthwaite to strictly safeguard the Company’s confidential information, prohibiting unauthorized use or disclosure, directly or indirectly. This includes all business, operational, and financial data. Upon request or upon ending his role, Satterthwaite must return all related records and documents. However, these obligations do not apply to information legitimately available in the public domain through no fault of Satterthwaite or his affiliates.

Other sections address waiver, amendment procedures, assignment restrictions, entire agreement status, governing law (Ohio), notice requirements, successors and assigns, cost allocation, and the incorporation of recitals. The agreement is signed by Satterthwaite, the Company, and Telecomm.

Proposition: Under certain circumstances, the Receiving Party is allowed to make copies of specific Confidential Information.

2. Each party designates representatives to facilitate the agreement.
3. Use of Confidential Information: The Receiving Party will utilize Confidential Information solely for specified purposes described in the agreement.

7. Exceptions: The agreement's restrictions do not apply to information the Receiving Party already knew in written form, information that becomes public without fault of the Receiving Party, information obtained from third parties without similar restrictions, information independently developed prior to receipt, information released by the Disclosing Party to others without restriction, information approved for release in writing by the Disclosing Party, information required to be disclosed by law or government order, or information revealed by inspecting a product after public disclosure or sale.

9. Standard of Care: The Receiving Party must protect Confidential Information with the same level of care it uses for its own confidential data, and at least a reasonable degree of care.
10. No License: No rights or licenses to patents, copyrights, or other intellectual property are granted except as necessary to use the information as authorized. There are no obligations to purchase, deal exclusively, or offer products for sale as a result of this agreement, and no partnership or joint venture is formed.

13. Governing Law: Michigan law governs this NDA.
14. Warranty & Liability: The Discloser warrants it has the right to share the Confidential Information but offers no further warranties, and all information is provided 'as is.' Neither party is liable for special, incidental, or consequential damages resulting from the use or disclosure of Confidential Information.
15. Entire Agreement: This document supersedes all prior understandings on the subject. Changes must be in writing and signed by authorized representatives.
16. Execution: Electronic signatures are valid and the agreement is legally binding.

Confidentiality agreement
OLCF Corporation PTE. LTD. is incorporated in Singapore and referred to as 'the Company.' The purchaser of tokens is defined as 'the Investor,' as per the terms of the OLPORTAL token sale public offer ('the Offer'). Both parties have executed this confidentiality agreement ('the Agreement') as outlined below.
1. Definitions and general terms
1.1. The Company acts as the Disclosing Party in this Agreement.
1.2. The Investor is designated as the Receiving Party.
1.3. An Investor’s Agent is an individual authorized by the Investor to access Proprietary Information.
1.4. Proprietary Information comprises any material of the Company labeled as 'Commercial Secret' or 'Confidential,' possessing actual or potential commercial significance due to its exclusivity, and transmitted to the Investor via written documentation, including secure electronic means. This includes business and financial plans, strategies, market insights, financial records, accounting (except as required by law), contracts, pricing, marketing, technical details, trade secrets, intellectual property, know-how, research, production schedules, concepts, and intellectual activity property (such as inventions, rationalization proposals, utility models, designs, industrial models, unregistered software, databases, and logos).
Information is not considered Proprietary if it is publicly available, was provided to third parties by the Company without restriction, or became public without fault of the Investor, or if the Investor can demonstrate prior possession before receipt from the Company, or if no confidentiality requirement was attached.
Information independently developed by the Investor without using Proprietary Information is also excluded.
Personal data protection and bank secrecy are not governed by this Agreement.
2. Scope
2.1. The Agreement’s primary objective is to ensure the secure handling of Proprietary Information by both parties.
2.2. The Company shares relevant Proprietary Information regarding the acquisition and use of OL-tokens during the OLPORTAL ICO with the Investor, including special terms granted at any stage, subject to the Offer and related documents, including smart-contract provisions.
3. Confidentiality standards
3.1. The Investor may disclose Proprietary Information only to those who require it to exercise rights under the Offer, provided they are informed of the Agreement and commit not to disclose it further. The Investor must maintain a list of Agents who have accessed Proprietary Information.
3.2. If the Investor fails to comply with section 3.1, the Company may revoke access and unilaterally terminate agreements related to the Offer.
3.3. In the event of conflicting confidentiality clauses across agreements, the current Agreement’s terms take precedence.
3.4. The Investor must safeguard Proprietary Information using measures at least as strong as those employed for their own confidential data.
3.5. Authorized Agents and the Investor must use Proprietary Information solely for its intended purpose and not for any other activities.
3.6. The Investor may create copies or summaries of Proprietary Information, marked accordingly, only as necessary. Accurate records of such materials and their locations must be kept, with access restricted to authorized Agents.
3.7. The Investor must ensure secure storage of information, preventing unauthorized access by anyone other than designated Agents.
3.8. If a disclosure to third parties occurs, the Investor is required to promptly notify the Company and describe loss mitigation actions.
4. Disclosure protocols
4.1. Should legal requirements necessitate disclosure, the Investor must immediately notify the Company in writing, specifying the requester, and disclose only within legal bounds.
5. Rights limitations
5.1. All information provided remains the Company’s property. Documents and copies must be returned or destroyed upon written request.
5.2. The Company can review the Investor’s information protection measures. Failure to provide details or insufficient protection allows the Company to refuse further disclosure or terminate related agreements unilaterally.
6. Liability
6.1. Any party breaching obligations must compensate the other for damages resulting from disclosure or misuse, as per Singapore law.
7. Duration
7.1. The Agreement becomes effective upon Investor’s acceptance and remains valid for five years after the Offer’s expiration, requiring confidentiality for that term.
8. Assignment
8.1. Rights and obligations cannot be transferred without prior written approval from the other party.
9. Miscellaneous
9.1. Disputes under this Agreement are subject to SIAC arbitration.
9.2. The Agreement is published at olportal.ai.
9.3. The Agreement is in English; the Investor is responsible for translations. The English version prevails in case of discrepancies.
9.4. The Agreement forms part of the Offer, and all Offer provisions apply to party relations.

Contract Provision: AGREEMENT FOR NON-DISCLOSURE AND CONFIDENTIALITY
Date:
Participants:
1. COAST2COAST (2007) LIMITED, operating as Room2Rent (“Room2Rent”)
2. (“the Recipient”)
Context:
A. Room2Rent has created a system dedicated to the construction and leasing of portable cabins (“the System”).
B. Room2Rent intends to share proprietary information about the System with the Recipient, so the Recipient can evaluate the possibility of becoming a Room2Rent franchisee (“the Due Diligence”).
C. Room2Rent deems this proprietary information valuable; thus, in exchange for access to it during Due Diligence, the Recipient enters into this Agreement.
Agreement Details:
1. Definitions and Interpretation
1.1 Singular and plural references are interchangeable as context dictates.
1.2 Definitions
Unless otherwise required by context, these definitions apply:
"Confidential Information" encompasses all data, directly or indirectly pertaining to the System, and related to Room2Rent’s operations, financials, assets, transactions, or trade secrets, disclosed by Room2Rent or acquired by the Recipient from Room2Rent or its affiliates, including (but not limited to):
(a) All forms of intellectual property, such as opinions, forecasts, concepts, designs, processes, plans, studies, data, reports, expertise, or similar assets;
(b) Any materials or documents—reports, analyses, forecasts, notes, manuals, letters, or otherwise, whether physically recorded or not;
(c) Trade Secrets as specified herein;
(d) Any aforementioned information provided to the Recipient prior to the signing of this Agreement.
“Representative” includes any officer or staff member of the Recipient, or any adviser retained for Due Diligence, authorized to receive Confidential Information under Clause 3.1.
“Trade Secrets” refer to Room2Rent’s industrially or commercially viable information, not publicly accessible, economically valuable, and subject to reasonable secrecy protections.
2. Confidentiality
2.1 Recipient must keep all Confidential Information strictly confidential and refrain from sharing it, except as explicitly allowed or after receiving Room2Rent’s written approval.
2.2 Recipient shall only use Confidential Information as needed for Due Diligence.
2.3 Recipient may not copy Confidential Information, except for necessary distribution to Representatives during Due Diligence, and only with Room2Rent’s written consent.
2.4 Recipient may only create notes or records related to Confidential Information if strictly required for Due Diligence.
2.5 Clauses 2.1–2.4 and 4.1(c) do not apply to:
(a) Information publicly available (except when due to breach);
(b) Info received legally from a third party;
(c) Disclosure required by law or court order, with Room2Rent’s guidance to minimize exposure.
3. Disclosure to Representatives
3.1 Recipient may share Confidential Information with Representatives if:
(a) Disclosure is essential for Due Diligence; and
(b) Representatives are identified in writing and Room2Rent consents.
3.2 Recipient is responsible for Representatives’ actions equivalent to Recipient’s own obligations.
4. Return and Destruction
4.1 Upon Room2Rent’s request, Recipient must:
(a) Return all materials containing Confidential Information;
(b) Erase Confidential Information from all electronic repositories;
(c) Cease all use of Confidential Information; and confirm compliance in writing.
5. Indemnity and Breach
5.1 Recipient must indemnify Room2Rent for all foreseeable claims, losses, damages, and costs (including legal fees) arising from breaches.
5.2 Injunctive relief may supplement damages for breaches.
5.3 Room2Rent may terminate any existing or future agreements in case of breach.
6. Disclaimer and Acknowledgments
6.1 Any intellectual property related to the System developed by Recipient must be disclosed and becomes Room2Rent’s exclusive property.
6.2 Room2Rent retains all legal and equitable rights in Confidential Information and Trade Secrets, including intellectual property.
6.3 Recipient accepts that Room2Rent makes no guarantees regarding the accuracy or completeness of Confidential Information, except its good faith disclosure.
6.4 Recipient acknowledges that theft of Trade Secrets is a crime under section 230 of the Crimes Act 1961, punishable up to five years imprisonment.
6.5 Theft of intellectual property, including Confidential Information, under the Crimes Act 1961 is punishable up to seven years imprisonment.
7. Other Terms
7.1 Room2Rent may inform third parties of this Agreement’s existence and terms.
7.2 Amendments must be in writing and agreed by all parties; delays in exercising rights are not waivers.
7.3 Parties’ rights and duties persist beyond transaction completion.
7.4 New Zealand law governs this Agreement; parties submit to its jurisdiction.
7.5 Invalidity of any term does not affect the remainder.
7.6 Terms bind and benefit successors and assigns.
7.7 Agreement remains binding regardless of other contracts or relationship changes.
7.8 Obligations are enforceable by Room2Rent, its affiliates, and under the Contracts (Privity) Act 1982.

Contractual Provision: Exhibit 99.3
RECIPROCAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
This document is executed as of the date last signed below (the “Effective Date”) between InsightPOS LLC, a New Mexico limited liability company with its principal office at 8228 Louisiana Blvd, NE, Suite A, Albuquerque NM 87113 (“Insight”), and NEXT GROUP HOLDING, a Florida corporation with a main mailing address at 1111 Brickell Avenue, Miami, FL 33131 (the “Second Party”).
WHEREAS, Insight and the Second Party (collectively, the “Parties”) wish to engage in conversations that may involve either Party furnishing the other with proprietary and confidential material (“Confidential Information”);
WHEREAS, Confidential Information may include, but is not restricted to, the following of each Party: (1) business strategies, all agreements, practices, and procedures; (2) employee, client, and vendor details; (3) innovations, techniques, products, patent filings, and intellectual property; or (4) plans, designs, blueprints, prototypes, instruments, software, technical data, and related materials;
ACCORDINGLY, the Parties agree as follows:
1. Confidential Information can be shared by either Party, provided it is identified as proprietary and confidential—either by labeling written documents, or, for oral disclosures or unmarked written items, by informing the other Party via oral, email, written, or other suitable means.
2. After being notified of the proprietary and confidential status of disclosed information, the receiving Party (“Recipient”) must, for three (3) years from the disclosure date, avoid sharing such Confidential Information with any contractor or external party without prior written permission, and must safeguard it with at least the same level of care as its own confidential data, but not less than reasonable care. The Recipient is responsible for making sure all its personnel with access to such information understand its confidential status and comply with this Agreement. In the event of any unauthorized disclosure or if required by subpoena or another legal mandate, the Recipient must promptly inform the disclosing Party.
3. All Confidential Information remains the exclusive property of the disclosing Party; nothing in this Agreement gives the other Party any rights to such information. The Recipient will comply with any request to promptly return or destroy all copies and associated notes. The Parties recognize that any public or unauthorized release of Confidential Information would cause irreparable harm, justifying injunctive relief and an award of damages as appropriate.
4. This Agreement does not restrict either Party from independently developing or acquiring products without use of the other’s Confidential Information. The disclosing Party acknowledges that the Recipient may independently develop content or receive similar information from other sources; provided the Recipient does not breach this Agreement, such activity is permitted.
5. Notwithstanding the above, information is not considered Confidential Information and no confidentiality obligation applies if such information:
(a) Was already known to the Recipient through a third party not bound by confidentiality;
(b) Becomes public through no fault of the Recipient or its representatives;
(c) Is independently created by the Recipient without reference to Confidential Information;
(d) Is released with the disclosing Party’s approval (to the extent permitted);
(e) Is disclosed as required by law or a government order.
6. This Agreement does not create an agency, partnership, joint venture, or similar affiliation between the Parties.
7. Neither Party will announce or reveal the existence or details of this Agreement without the other’s consent.
8. This document constitutes the entire agreement and does not obligate either Party to exchange information or enter into further arrangements.
9. The Agreement remains effective for two (2) years from the Effective Date unless earlier terminated by notice. The requirement to safeguard Confidential Information survives termination.

Contract Excerpt: MICROSOFT CORPORATION RECIPROCAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
This document, referred to as the "Agreement," is entered into on the later of the two signing dates between Microsoft (China) Co., Ltd., a PRC corporation, and ATA Testing Authority, Beijing Co., Ltd., also a PRC corporation. The Agreement governs the exchange and protection of confidential information between the parties. Confidential Information is defined as any nonpublic data that the Disclosing Party either marks as confidential or that, by the nature of its disclosure, should reasonably be treated as confidential by the Receiving Party. This definition encompasses both tangible and intangible data related to unreleased or released products, marketing strategies, business practices, and third-party information that the Disclosing Party is obligated to keep confidential. Affiliates of both parties are included within the scope of Disclosing and Receiving Parties, as specified. Information excluded from Confidential Information includes that which becomes public through lawful means, was already known by the Receiving Party, is acquired from a third party without breach of obligation, is independently developed, or constitutes Feedback as detailed in Section 5. The Receiving Party is required to protect and restrict dissemination of Confidential Information for five years from the initial disclosure date, exercise at least reasonable care in its protection, limit use to business purposes, and avoid reverse engineering except where allowed by law. Disclosure to government entities is permitted only under certain conditions, such as prior notice or written assurances regarding protection, but computer source code is subject to stricter requirements. Confidential Information may be shared internally with employees and consultants provided they are bound by suitable written agreements. Breaches must be reported immediately, and all Confidential Information must be returned or destroyed upon request. The Agreement allows for injunctive relief for unauthorized disclosures. Ownership of Confidential Information remains with the Disclosing Party, and no rights to intellectual property are granted unless explicitly stated. Products provided as Confidential Information are for evaluation and feedback purposes only, and are supplied "AS IS" without warranties. Export laws and regulations must be followed. The Agreement does not limit either party’s ability to independently develop products, and residuals retained in memory may be used freely, provided Confidential Information is not disclosed. Feedback is voluntary and, unless a separate agreement exists, does not impose confidentiality obligations on the receiver. Legal disputes are subject to CIETAC arbitration in Beijing under PRC law. The Agreement is binding on successors and assigns, subject to written approval for assignment. If any provision is deemed unenforceable, the remainder stays effective. Either party may terminate with ninety days’ written notice, but confidentiality obligations survive termination. Suggestions and Feedback may be freely used by the receiver, absent any separate agreement. The Agreement concludes with signatures from representatives of both parties.

Statement: Confidential Information is restricted solely to technical data.
